detail.abstract: Martin Hearson's Imposing Standards asks why lower-income countries have signed tax treaties contrary to their long-term interests. Drawing on seventy-five interviews and case studies of the United Kingdom, Zambia, Vietnam and Cambodia, Hearson contends that the complexity of international tax confers authority on those whose command of it is recognized: tax competition operates as a social rather than a material fact, the so-called tax treaties myth, and a transnational policy community centered at the OECD reifies norms injurious to the distributional interests of capital-importing states. This review lauds a qualitative historical method that is a rarity in a subfield dominated by empirical and doctrinal studies, and canvasses the book's contribution to the literatures on epistemic communities and policy diffusion. Two reservations follow. The case against tax competition rests on secondary studies and meta-analyses for want of original data, and the treaty network is taken to be hard law without engaging the extant debate over whether an international tax regime exists at all. That debate is consequential: if tax remains the fundamental purchase of states, the hegemonic status of the OECD's norms is less secure than Imposing Standards allows.

title: Has AI Assassinated God? Technology, Secularism, and the Death of the Divine

detail.title: Has AI Assassinated God? Technology, Secularism, and the Death of the Divine

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Nietzsche's declaration that "God is dead" was not a celebration of atheism but a warning about what happens when a society loses the transcendent authority that once organized its moral and existential life. This paper asks whether artificial intelligence is becoming one of the forces filling that void. I argue that AI is doing more than accelerating secularization: it is increasingly taking on roles once associated with the divine. As people turn to AI for answers, guidance, companionship, and even visions of digital immortality, machines are becoming new sources of knowledge, moral judgment, emotional support, and hope. Drawing on philosophy, sociology, theology, and cultural analysis, the paper examines this shift across four dimensions: epistemological, psychological, moral, and existential. It considers how algorithms can function like oracles, how AI companions can reshape practices of care and prayer, how automated systems can influence ethical decisions, and how promises of digital consciousness can resemble a secular form of salvation. The paper does not claim that AI has literally killed God or that religion has disappeared. Rather, it asks whether AI is changing the cultural conditions through which belief, authority, meaning, and transcendence are understood-and what this transformation means for religion, democracy, and human life in America.

detail.abstract: Retail futures evaluations are often compared by nominal account size, profit target, maximum drawdown and purchase price. Those fields are insufficient to identify the contract. This paper constructs a versioned atlas whose unit of observation is the provider-product-route-size-stage-version tuple. Three public directories and official-site discovery define a frame of 23 futures providers. Official provider sources support 177 current or explicitly retained product-route-size configurations across 22 providers on 5 September 2026; one discovered provider remains unresolved. The catalogue retains every size and route whose core geometry can be verified, while missing fields remain visible rather than being set to zero. It separates evaluation, simulated funded and live transitions and records EOD, intraday and static drawdown, daily stops, consistency, minimum days, payout hurdles and route choices. A common-path Monte Carlo engine supplies scenario-conditional probabilities for 155 evaluation configurations and 103 funded configurations with sufficient inputs, producing 774 stage-scenario results. It does not estimate observed company pass or payout rates. The analysis reports all coded account sizes, from 25K to 300K, and shows that nominal size is not itself the causal input: target-to-loss-budget ratios and stage-specific restrictions determine the modeled differences. In a matched LucidDaily comparison, evaluation pass probability falls from 48.02% at 25K to 28.55% at 150K as the target-to-drawdown ratio rises, whereas conditional first-payout eligibility rises from 38.63% to 51.96% as the funded hurdle-to-drawdown ratio falls. The workbook reports every product-level result together with its standard error, Wilson interval, path count, success count, horizon, monitoring grid and seed. Lim (2026a) reports 31 contracts across 21 firms; the present futures-only corpus reaches comparable provider breadth while retaining substantially more within-provider routes and sizes. The contribution is a stage-specific, version-aware data architecture and executable rule taxonomy that makes product coverage, model coverage and remaining uncertainty auditable.

detail.abstract: Supply chain practices are commonly analyzed as independent predictors, although firms often implement them as bundles. This paper evaluates whether heterogeneous configurations of internal integration, supplier integration, digitalization, analytics, sustainability, and security-resilience can be recovered through latent-profile analysis and linked to operational, financial-resilience, and environmental outcomes. A reproducible synthetic dataset of 700 analytical firm cases was generated from three underlying capability archetypes. Gaussian mixture models with two to six profiles were compared using Bayesian and Akaike information criteria and silhouette statistics. The three-profile solution had the lowest BIC (7,430.82) and recovered cost-centered, digital-resilient, and integration-centered profiles. Profile membership explained 48.9% of operationalperformance variation, 53.3% of financial-resilience variation, and 54.0% of environmental-performance variation. The digital-resilient profile achieved the strongest financial and environmental outcomes, while the integration-centered profile achieved similar operational performance but weaker financial-resilience and environmental results. The cost-centered profile was below the sample mean on every capability and outcome. The study demonstrates a transparent configurational measurement pipeline; it does not estimate the distribution or performance of actual Egyptian firms. AI use disclosure. detail.abstract: Cities face an increasingly urgent need to adapt to climate risks and mitigate the disparate impacts of climate change. Emergent data-driven policy innovations, known as building performance standards, establish targets for building carbon emissions and energy consumption over time as means to lower emissions, increase community resilience capacity, and improve public health. Achieving these targets will require significant building retrofit and electrification investments. Given growing concerns around housing and energy costs and the uncertain pace of grid decarbonization, we analyze the affordability and equity implications of building performance standards and the pathways to achieve policy goals. Focusing our analysis New York City's Local Law 97, we examine energy and emissions data for more than 35,000 buildings over ten years, along with detailed energy audit data for a subset of 5,681 buildings. We develop a multi-scalar empirical model of the cost and distribution of carbon emissions reductions at the building, neighborhood, and city scales over time, and use machine learning models to predict the likelihood of meeting carbon intensity targets. We specifically explore the impacts of building decarbonization for subsidized housing and disadvantaged communities. Our results show that while building performance standards can accelerate the reduction of energy use and emissions in cities, uncertainties around future grid decarbonization, energy prices, and building electrification costs necessitate a data-driven approach that can reduce retrofit barriers for owners, respond to changing technology adoption rates and economic signals, and quantify the environmental and public health co-benefits of decarbonization strategies, particularly for disadvantaged communities.

title: Taxation and Formal Equality

detail.title: Taxation and Formal Equality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Laws of contemporary capitalist democracies share an important trait: With few notable but limited exceptions, legal rules make no formal distinctions between the rich and the poor. A multi-millionaire and a minimum wage worker alike may cast only one vote, must stop at a red light, have to pay the same sales tax, and can send their kids to a public school for free. Such formal equality of modern legal regimes is no accident. Formal equality influenced ideas and laws of classical Greece and ancient Rome, it inspired Enlightenment thinkers, it motivated constitutional revisions in many American states, and it shapes contemporary proposals for egalitarian reforms. This Article posits that formal equality influences policymaking in liberal democracies and investigates the implications of this argument for the design of the tax-and-transfer system. These implications extend to the choice of tax base, the design of transfer programs, the timing of income recognition, the taxation of capital gains and inter-generational transfers, and a host of other tax and tax-adjacent policies ranging from corporate integration to the minimum wage. The overall lesson is that the constraints imposed by formal equality do not necessarily make the tax-and-transfer system less progressive, but they do shape the choices faced by the advocates of progressive tax reforms, today and in the future.

detail.abstract:
The purpose of this paper is to introduce a fully integrated, risk-informed, probabilistic framework
that carries over seamlessly from enterprise portfolio decision making to operational risk and
opportunity management. It accomplishes both functions by adhering to seven principles and
premises: (1) that quantitative, probabilistic risk analysis and management methods need to be
used not only at the level of projects and programs, but also for enterprise portfolio planning and
execution; (2) that success at enterprise level requires continuously considering not only the
financial, safety, security, and technical gains that emanate from mission accomplishment, but
also potential aspirational gains that are not directly quantifiable at the time planning occurs; (3)
that the consideration of aspirational gains requires tapping into stakeholder insights and tacit
knowledge by introducing and applying affective performance measures (e.g., degrees of
enthusiasm or concern); (4) that the risk of slippages of critical milestones should be a key
element of the analysis; (5) that the first four premises motivate the use of Monte Carlo methods
to account for all important sources of uncertainty; (6) that the Monte Carlo formulation should
incorporate quantitative-qualitative hybrid models where needed to address the aspirational
objectives; and (7) that the hybrid models should be informed by eliciting the judgments of both
the organization’s stakeholders (i.e., executive management, staff, customers, and partners) and
external entities that benefit from or are affected by the operation (e.g., scientists, educators, and
the public). The importance of treating both the planning and execution using the same basic
analytical framework is emphasized throughout.

detail.abstract: Pavement management in the United States and internationally remains predominantly reliant on periodic manual inspection, a paradigm that the academic literature and federal engineering guidance alike identify as structurally inadequate to the scale and complexity of modern road networks. Over the past decade, three parallel streams of innovation have emerged to address this gap: machine-learning-based analytics applied to existing condition data, embedded and on-surface sensor technologies for continuous structural monitoring, and cognitive digital twin architectures that integrate real-time data with predictive modeling. This paper reviews the state of the art across these three streams, situates existing commercial pavement management platforms within this landscape, and presents a detailed technical description of an Intelligent Digital Monitoring System (IDMS)-protected under USPTO Provisional Patent Application No. 64/116,669-that integrates embedded IoT pavement sensors, machine-learning-based predictive analytics, and geospatial decision-support dashboards into a single interoperable architecture. The analysis finds that, while individual components of this architecture have been separately validated in the academic literature and separately commercialized by point-solution vendors, no reviewed commercial platform combines continuous embedded sensing, network-level machine-learning prediction, and real-time geospatial decision support within a single system calibrated to FHWA-defined pavement condition categories. The paper concludes by identifying this integration gap as the specific technical contribution of the disclosed system.

detail.abstract: The Nifty 50 has evolved from an index covering roughly a third of NSE's listed market capitalisation at its 1996 launch into the primary benchmark index for Indian equity markets. The index anchors approximately ₹4.89 trillion in domestic passive assets and has become one of the world's most heavily traded index-derivatives franchises. This paper examines the nature and relevance of the index's construction rules. The paper critiques four structural limitations present in the index: uncapped single-stock and sector concentration, the divergence of the index's sectoral weights from India's gross value-added composition, liquidity-and size-based rebalancing rules, and mandatory derivatives-eligibility gating. Drawing primarily on NSE's disclosures, regulatory filings, and the academic literature on index effects, this paper contrasts these findings against comparable global benchmarks and argues that the Nifty 50 functions less as a representative economic proxy and more as a liquidity-weighted portfolio of India's largest formal-sector firms. The observations and findings of the paper call for further enquiry and regular examination of the relevance, soundness, and alignment of the underlying index construction rules with the index's true objectives.

title: Psychological Models, Modalities, and Human Factors In Conflict Frameworks in Conflict Resolution and Law

detail.title: Psychological Models, Modalities, and Human Factors In Conflict Frameworks in Conflict Resolution and Law

detail.abstract:
Abstract

Conflict is more than substantive disagreement; it carries an emotional, psychological, and relational dimension that legal training alone does not fully address. This paper argues that conflict resolution cannot function as a purely legal exercise because legal disputes involve human needs, developmental histories, unconscious dynamics, emotional responses, relationships, power structures, and institutional conditions.

The paper distinguishes between psychological models and modalities. Models, including Maslow, Erikson, Freud, and Jung, provide interpretive frameworks for understanding the needs, developmental experiences, unconscious processes, defenses, and projections that influence conflict. Modalities, including Dialectical Behavior Therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, Internal Family Systems, Interpersonal Therapy, and systems or organizational approaches, provide practical methods for addressing emotional dysregulation, relational disruption, communication breakdowns, trauma responses, and recurring structural conflict.

The paper also examines human factors, including the nervous system, neurobiology, and trauma, and explains how these factors influence threat perception, emotional regulation, memory, communication, decision-making, and participation in legal and conflict-resolution processes. This analysis is connected to established conflict-resolution frameworks, including the work of Dayton and Kriesberg, Rahim, Elgoibar, Euwema and Munduate, Lipsitz, and Deutsch.

The real-world application section applies these models, modalities, and human-factor principles across nine areas of law. It demonstrates how psychological insight can inform custody and parenting disputes in family law, accountability and trauma-informed practice in criminal law, legitimacy and safety in administrative and immigration matters, emotional regulation and role conflict in employment disputes, and the identity, grief, authority, and relational dynamics underlying civil, constitutional, business, corporate, and commercial conflicts.

The paper concludes that legal doctrine can resolve a case without resolving the human conflict underneath it. Law and psychology are therefore not separate disciplines competing for relevance; they are complementary forms of professional knowledge. Integrating psychological models, practical modalities, and human-factor awareness can help legal and conflict-resolution professionals distinguish legal issues from the deeper conditions that sustain conflict and develop outcomes that are not only legally sound but also psychologically informed and more durable.

detail.abstract: Place-based innovation policies increasingly commit public resources to a particular industry. We ask whether such policies shape entrepreneurial entry beyond the fundamentals they provide, by redirecting founders' attention toward the targeted industry. We exploit staggered accelerator launches by the Creative Destruction Lab, a global mentorship program, each targeting one science-based industry in one city, and link program records to startup and founder data. Following a launch, entry into the targeted industry rises relative to other local industries. The response is concentrated among science-trained first-time founders and among industries with little prior local presence. We develop and estimate a model of entrepreneurial industry choice that uses serial founders as an informed benchmark to distinguish consideration from payoff spillovers. The counterfactual estimates imply that consideration accounts for 22.8 percent of science-trained first-time entry into targeted industries. Place-based innovation policy can therefore shape the trajectory of technological change not only through the resources it provides, but also by directing entrepreneurs' attention toward targeted industries.

title: Dethroning the Dollar? Optimal Multi-Asset Market Making *
affiliations: University of Toronto and McMaster University - Michael G. DeGroote School of Business

detail.title: Dethroning the Dollar? Optimal Multi-Asset Market Making *

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not applicable

Andreas gratefully acknowledges financial support from SSHRC (grant number 435-2026-0281), the Rotman School of Management's Finhub, and the Canadian Securities Institute Research Foundation.

detail.abstract: Most foreign exchange transactions route through the U.S. dollar, even when the parties want to exchange two other currencies. Vehicle routing concentrates volume in dollar markets and lowers their trading costs, but a cross-currency trade pays fees and price impact on two dollar legs. We ask whether a single liquidity pool that makes markets in several currencies can lower aggregate trading costs. The designer chooses the capital weights across currencies and the fee on each pair. With competitive liquidity provision and aggregate fee revenue set optimally, the weights determine aggregate trading costs and each pair's price impact; the division of fees across pairs determines how those costs are shared by traders. We characterize the optimal weights and derive a closed-form condition under which some choice of weights yields lower aggregate costs than vehicle routing: the volume-weighted sum of pairwise return correlations and cross-currency flow intensities must be positive. The routing cost is a boundary value of the pool's cost function as its dollar share approaches one. We also characterize the fee schedules that deter entry by a dedicated dollar market and show that aggregate dominance does not guarantee robustness to entry. Foreign exchange is our main application, but the results apply to any set of assets traded against a common settlement asset.

title: A Survey of the Mathematization of the Factor Hierarchy Law : Formalization of the Three Axioms, the Cross-Disciplinary Verification Matrix, and a Preliminary Establishment Statement

detail.title: A Survey of the Mathematization of the Factor Hierarchy Law : Formalization of the Three Axioms, the Cross-Disciplinary Verification Matrix, and a Preliminary Establishment Statement

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract:
The Factor Hierarchy Law (Tang, 2026g) consists of three axioms: Axiom 1 (Factor Dichotomy), Axiom 2 (Regime Switching/Structural Break), and Axiom 3 (Interaction Effect). This law has been systematically verified in six completely independent disciplines, but the mathematical formalization of the three axioms has been missing until now. This paper surveys the three papers of the Factor Hierarchy Law mathematization series (Tang, 2026am–2026ao) and formally declares that the three axioms have acquired a complete mathematical foundation within the k-regime linear switching model.

Formalization of Axiom 1 (Tang, 2026am): the Switching Type Classification Theorem proves that the parameter difference between any adjacent regimes must be one of three types—pure slope switching (corresponding to a pure regime factor), full-parameter switching (corresponding to a dual-identity factor), or pure intercept switching (corresponding to a pure execution factor)—and the fourth combination is excluded by switching existence. The Exhaustiveness Theorem for Six Hierarchical Structures proves that the hierarchical structure within the standard model belongs to one and only one of four types (single-layer system, single-switching system, multi-switching system, dual-switching system); after introducing additional moderating variables, hierarchical switching systems and cyclic switching systems may arise, and the six types jointly exhaust all possibilities. The Completeness Theorem for the Switching Type Sequence proves that the sequence is a bijective invariant of the hierarchical partial order. Numerical verification discovers two original phenomena: the discretization plateau effect and the sample-size sensitivity of weak-effect-size classification.

Formalization of Axiom 2 (Tang, 2026an): the Geometric Necessity of Rupture Theorem proves that the unified shape function exhibits a cusp at the true boundary, with a strictly positive slope jump. The Local Uniqueness of the Critical Value Theorem proves that each true boundary is a locally unique maximum point. The Rupture Strength–Slope Jump Correspondence Theorem establishes the explicit relation between J(τ*) and ‖Δθ‖_Σ². The cusp sharpness index R(τ*) = J/h provides a geometric measure depending only on the boundary location and density. The Cascade Transmission Efficiency Theorem reveals the monotone relation between the effect size ratio and the cascade alignment precision.

Formalization of Axiom 3 (Tang, 2026ao): the η Divergence Theorem proves that the limiting behavior of η must be one of 0, a finite positive number, or ∞. The η Limit Theorem for Three Morphologies precisely characterizes the η limiting behavior of the three switching types. The proposition on the η trajectory of a processual variable proves that η exhibits a plateau (rather than a peak) in a neighborhood of the boundary along the regime variable, with the plateau value proportional to the square of the slope Switching Degree. The Geometric Interpretation Theorem for η interprets the finite limit of η as the squared tangent of the direction angle of the switching difference vector: η* = tan²φ.

This paper presents a Preliminary Establishment Statement: within the k-regime linear switching model (A0–A8), the three axioms of the Factor Hierarchy Law have all been mathematically formalized; the exhaustiveness of the three-way switching type classification and the six hierarchical structures has been proved; and testable definitions of the extended configurations have been provided. This paper also gives a cross-disciplinary verification matrix, mapping the three axioms to empirical findings in six disciplines; consolidates open problems FHL-T1 through FHL-T23; and provides a concrete list of tools for the subsequent Information Isomorphism Law mathematization series.

The core methodology, research direction, and final decisions were independently directed by the author. DeepSeek assisted with code implementation, data presentation, and text drafting. The author takes full academic responsibility for the final content.

detail.abstract: Monopoly power, economic moats, durable quality: four exchange-traded funds promise some version of the same idea. Do they deliver the same portfolio? We compare MPLY, MOAT, TOLL and the now-closed CZAR, first through their documented strategies and observed returns, then through a simulation of the stocks they recently held. The common live history is short, so we run a separate counterfactual from January 2016 to September 2026, asking how those holdings would have behaved under buy-and-hold and under monthly rebalancing. The results are less about the theme than about a few individual winners. Under buy-and-hold, Nvidia alone accounts for 71.5% of MPLY's total gain and 61.4% of MOAT's. One stock. Rebalancing monthly cuts those direct shares to 21.5% and 11.2%, and replacing each basket's largest contributor with cash still leaves annualized returns of 24.40%, 15.66%, 23.04% and 13.32%, respectively. The rankings themselves move with the starting date. None of this establishes a causal monopoly premium, and a replay of recent holdings cannot reconstruct what managers actually did. What it does show is more useful: one theme, four very different portfolios, with returns decided by the stocks behind the label.

title: Do Market-Wide Circuit Breakers Calm the Markets or Panic Them?
affiliations: Deakin University,  and University of Melbourne - Melbourne Business School

detail.abstract: We examine the effectiveness of market-wide circuit breakers (MWCBs) by comparing market quality between four instances of trading halts during COVID-19 and other significant market declines in March 2020, as well as the 2008 global financial crisis. We find that MWCBs affect different investors and different stocks in different ways. First, liquidity and price discovery deteriorate immediately after market reopening but recover within a short period of time. Second, trading volume rises sharply, and buy-side support strengthens especially among the most distressed stocks, driven by non-retail investors. Third, price discovery recovers faster for stocks listed on the NYSE than for those listed on the Nasdaq. Fourth, market quality worsens while retail trading surges and liquidity providers withdraw as the index approaches the trading halt thresholds, consistent with a magnet effect. Overall, MWCBs disrupt market quality in the short term, but non-retail participants, rather than retail investors, absorb the post-halt selling pressure and stabilize the markets thereafter.

detail.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly power financial conversational assistants, detecting investment advice in natural language has become a critical regulatory and safety challenge. Unlike explicit single-turn recommendations, investment advice often emerges implicitly and progressively over multi-turn conversations, shaped by user intent, delivery style, and contextual buildup. We introduce the first comprehensive framework for detecting both sequential and contextual investment advice in dialogue settings. Central to our approach is a modular, top-down synthetic data generation pipeline that systematically spans a taxonomy of advisory trajectories using an axis-bucket-descriptor schema. We simulate both benign and high-risk conversations across diverse user personas, financial instruments, and risk tiers, and evaluate detection capabilities using LLM-as-a-Judge with entropy-based uncertainty diagnostics. Our results show that contextual advisory detection remains substantially more challenging than sequential cases, even under few-shot prompting with tailored demonstrations. This work lays the foundation for scalable guardrail development in highstakes, compliance-sensitive domains, where advisory risk is often subtle, distributed, and perception-dependent.

title: The Representative First Amendment: Public-Sector Exclusive Representation After Janus v. AFSCME

detail.title: The Representative First Amendment: Public-Sector Exclusive Representation After Janus v. AFSCME

publicationDetails.journalName: Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Exclusive representation is at the heart of U.S. labor law. Yet despite its centrality, dicta in the Supreme Court's Janus v. American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees, Council 31 decision and antilabor litigants seeking to build on the case threaten to kill the doctrine. The weapon of choice: the First Amendment. As numerous commentators have noted, the Supreme Court's First Amendment jurisprudence has become a sword for slashing regulations in recent years. Janus furthered this trend by striking down agency fees. With ever more robust protections afforded against compelled speech and association, exclusive representation appears slated to be the next victim. Nothing is inevitable about these developments. Examining the context and consequences of Janus for both exclusive representation in public-sector unions and public-sector workplaces, this Note uncovers an alternative interpretation of the First Amendment wherein the rights it articulates act as a shield for representative practices. Deemed the "representative First Amendment, " this Note details the normative roots and jurisprudential contours of this interpretation, ironically tracing these aspects out from the very developments that led to Janus. Although methodologically the interpretive tasks ahead require pulling together strands of political and legal theory related to the nature of democratic representation, the goal is practical: to analyze public-sector exclusive representation from the vantage point of the representative First Amendment and determine whether the former survives the scrutiny of the latter. As this Note concludes, exclusive representation is safe under this interpretation.

title: The 10 Forces Shaping Our Future: Planetary Megatrends, Global Problems, and Emerging Threats to Technological Civilization

detail.title: The 10 Forces Shaping Our Future: Planetary Megatrends, Global Problems, and Emerging Threats to Technological Civilization

detail.abstract: This report proposes an integrated analytical architecture for understanding global change: a six-layer causal chain running from ten planetary megatrends, through structural pressures and present-day global problems, to emerging threats and, ultimately, global and systemic risks. Rather than treating megatrends, problems, threats, and risks as interchangeable items on a single list-as much of the global-risk literature implicitly does-the framework organizes them as distinct layers of a dynamic, many-to-many causal system, and formalizes the resulting distinction between conditions that are already observable (problems) and developments that may materialize or intensify in the future (threats). Building on two decades of the author's independent research, the report defines and characterizes ten megatrends spanning demography, ecology, public health, security, finance, technology and governance; maps their pairwise interactions; traces their connection to roughly fifty candidate global problems and two dozen candidate emerging threats; and situates global catastrophic and existential risk as the terminal segment of this longer causal chain rather than as a freestanding subject. A concluding section proposes an operationalization path-a set of roughly 100-150 planetary vital signs-for converting the framework into a continuously monitorable observatory of global change. The analysis is offered as an exploratory, think-tank-style contribution for investors, policymakers, and technology and risk analysts, not as a probabilistic forecast.

title: Subjective Survival Probability in Mortality and Longevity Risks: A Cross-Disciplinary Review
affiliations: and National University of Singapore

detail.abstract: Subjective survival probabilities (SSPs) capture people's reported chances of surviving to a specified age, linking perceived mortality risk to retirement, insurance, and longevity-related decisions. This review synthesises 57 papers across economics, demography, actuarial science, and health research. It examines how SSPs are elicited, shaped by health and socioeconomic conditions, affected by response patterns, and used in mortality prediction and economic models. SSPs respond to health information, reflect health and socioeconomic gradients, and add predictive value for mortality. Yet they are noisy and imperfectly calibrated: focal responses, rounding, inconsistency, and nonresponse limit interpretation and cross-survey comparison. Importantly, when compared with objective survival probabilities (OSPs), an SSP-OSP gap should not automatically be treated as measurement error. Instead, we outline that the gap can reflect private information, expected cohort mortality improvement, systematic optimism or pessimism, and reporting effects. SSPs are therefore most useful alongside objective mortality models in risk assessment, retirement communication, annuity research, and longevity-product valuation.

detail.abstract: We report strong out-of-sample statistical evidence in favor of a universal multi-currency manifold of interest rate levels for which rate shocks lie in locally deterministic tangent planes. The manifolds estimated from rate levels closely match the integral manifolds of shock k-planes in both linear and nonlinear cases. For a nine-currency panel combining XIBOR and OIS histories, the advantage of currency pooling (i.e., aggregating historical data across multiple currencies and index types) is seen across all in-sample/out-of-sample splits and is especially large when the out-of-sample period was subject to a different monetary policy than the in-sample period. Based on these results, we propose the use of currency pooling over combined XIBOR and OIS histories for estimating curve basis representations and mean reversion rates, while using currency- and index-specific calibration for volatility.

detail.abstract: Global tax governance is undergoing a structural transformation, expanding from traditional issues of base erosion, profit shifting, and tax competition toward interconnected governance challenges that encompass carbon pricing, climate finance, border carbon adjustments, digital economy taxation, and international tax cooperation. As of 2026, direct carbon pricing policies cover slightly more than 29% of global greenhouse gas emissions, generating over USD 107 billion in public revenue in 2025-a more than threefold increase from less than USD 30 billion in 2016. The global average direct carbon price stands at nearly USD 21 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent, double the level of a decade ago. Concurrently, the OECD global minimum tax regime is advancing into further implementation and coordination phases, and the United Nations Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation entered its fifth substantive negotiating session in August 2026. Global tax and climate governance are forming an increasingly complex institutional network.

detail.abstract: As organizations adopt multiple artificial intelligence (AI) services, consumption-based pricing creates a measurement problem that conventional cost dashboards do not resolve. Tokens, credits, API calls, compute time, and agent actions describe resource use, but they do not establish whether the resulting work produces organizational value. This article develops the AI Consumption Value Model (ACVM), a conceptual framework that connects AI consumption to activity, a business-defined unit of work, operational outcomes, multidimensional value, and an investment decision. The model is developed through conceptual synthesis of research on information technology business value, benefits realization, activity-based costing, technology unit economics, and empirical evidence on generative AI productivity. ACVM distinguishes economic, capacity, performance, and strategic value; treats released time as capacity rather than automatic financial savings; allocates multi-provider AI costs to workflows rather than requiring single-vendor attribution; and introduces marginal value as a basis for scaling decisions. An illustrative enterprise service-management scenario demonstrates how the model can move analysis from cost per token toward cost per successful outcome while preserving quality, risk, and human judgment as explicit considerations. The article proposes measures and testable propositions for future empirical validation. ACVM is intended as a decision framework rather than a universal return-on-investment formula, allowing organizations to define value relative to their own work, baseline performance, and strategic priorities.

detail.abstract: The adoption of online monitoring tools has become increasingly relevant in enhancing project management activities in government organizations, particularly in ensuring efficiency, transparency, and accountability. This study examined the relationship between the adoption of online monitoring tools and project management effectiveness in a Philippine government agency, focusing on 135 employees who are directly involved in projectbased activities. Employing a descriptive-correlational quantitative research design, data were gathered through a researcher-structured questionnaire and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and Pearson's correlation coefficient as statistical tools. The findings revealed a high level of adoption of online monitoring tools in terms of task tracking, progress reporting, coordination and collaboration, and information accessibility, as well as a high level of project management effectiveness in terms of timeliness of project completion, accuracy of monitoring and reporting, resource utilization, and coordination among project team members. Results further showed that all dimensions of online monitoring tools adoption were significantly correlated with all dimensions of project management effectiveness, indicating that increased use of digital monitoring platforms is associated with improved project outcomes. Based on the findings of this study, a strategy roadmap is proposed to strengthen the adoption of online monitoring tools and enhance project management effectiveness in government agencies. This study provides practical insights for government agencies seeking to improve project performance through the strategic use of digital monitoring systems.

detail.abstract: We review the evidence on subsidized job training programs in industrial countries. We provide critical, narrative summaries of randomized studies of major job training in the US; of two “judge randomization” studies in the US and Denmark; and of previous meta-analyses. We then perform a meta-analysis of 56 randomized trials of job training in the US since 1973, the most exhaustive meta-analysis in this niche. Here, average impacts are positive but modest: employment rises 1.7 percentage points in years 3–5, and annual pre-tax earnings by roughly $800 per person offered training. At an average cost of $13,598 per participant, programs roughly break even under (debatable) assumptions about how long benefits persist. They recoup about three-quarters of their cost for government through higher tax revenue and lower benefit use. Evaluations of the largest federal efforts—JTPA, the Workforce Investment Act, and Job Corps—return small or null effects. One cluster of programs stands out: "sector programs," which screen applicants intensively, design curricula with employers, and track local skill demand. They raise earnings roughly ten times as much. They have proven difficult to replicate.

detail.abstract: Identifying the impact of capital inflows on output is challenging because inflows are forward-looking and respond to expectations about future economic conditions. We develop a new measure of capital inflow shocks using a simple and broadly applicable expectations-based framework that isolates the unexpected component of inflows by purging movements predicted by professional forecasters' expectations. Estimates using the new measure for 27 emerging market economies indicate that capital inflows have sizable expansionary effects on output, operating through stronger domestic consumption and investment and easier financing conditions. Additional analysis indicates that equitytype inflows generate greater and more persistent effects than debt-type inflows, while large inflow reversals result in more pronounced effects than comparable increases in inflows. These results are robust to a wide range of alternative specifications.

detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the shift toward contactless payments, yet cash demand remained persistent. This paper examines whether this persistent cash dependence during the pandemic reflects limited access to alternative payment instruments or limited digital capability. Using the 2021 Bank of Korea Survey of Payment Methods and Mobile Financial Services, we show that digitally literate consumers are more likely to reduce cash holdings and increase mobile-app payments during the pandemic. The difference between digitally literate and illiterate consumers persists even after controlling for financial access, payment-instrument bundles, and local characteristics, including socialdistancing stringency. While stricter social distancing corresponds to greater mobile-app payments, it is not associated with reductions in cash holdings. These results suggest that digital literacy is a key determinant of consumers' reliance on cash during the pandemic.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between Bangladesh's prolonged natural-gas and electricity shortages and the performance of the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) during 2025 and 2026. Using secondary data drawn from Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics releases, Bangladesh Bank and Petro Bangla-related news reporting, and DSE trading records reported in the national business press, the study assembles a chronological account of major energysupply disruptions and matches it against corresponding movements in the DSEX benchmark index, sectoral output figures, and single-session trading data. The analysis finds that periods of acute gas curtailment-particularly the four-week crisis that began on 21 July 2026coincided with a sustained index decline of 345 points and a single-session loss of Tk 6,781 crore in market capitalization on 6 September 2026, alongside a slowdown in industrial GDP growth from 3.71 to 2.86 percent. The paper argues that the sell-off was broad-based rather than confined to energy-intensive sectors, pointing to a general investor-confidence channel operating alongside a direct corporate-earnings channel. The study is descriptive-analytical in design, given its reliance on publicly available secondary data rather than proprietary highfrequency trading data, and it concludes with recommendations for regulators, listed firms, and future researchers.

detail.abstract: The full-scale war has triggered profound structural changes in the Ukrainian economy, creating the need not only for the physical reconstruction of destroyed infrastructure, but also for a fundamental rethinking of the country's longterm development model. Under conditions of limited fiscal resources, demographic decline, persistent security uncertainty, and dependence on external assistance, traditional postwar recovery strategies are likely to prove insufficient. This article develops an analytically grounded framework for adapting the principles of economic experimentation and the experience of China's special economic zones-particularly the Shenzhen model-to the Ukrainian context. It argues that mechanisms of experimental regulation, embedded autonomy of the developmental state, and institutionalised policy learning can be selectively adapted to a democratic postconflict economy, provided that they are embedded within transparent, rulesbased governance structures. The proposed model of multipolar development clusters is conceptualised as a mechanism for concentrating resources, reducing institutional uncertainty, and accelerating integration into global value chains. By linking economic experimentation with regional differentiation and international anchoring, the framework offers a pathway for combining rapid recovery with longterm structural transformation. The article contributes to the literature on postconflict reconstruction, comparative political economy, and special economic zones by advancing a conceptually coherent approach to institutional adaptation. It provides a foundation for designing pilot zones and development clusters not merely as policy instruments, but as platforms for iterative learning, innovation, and sustained economic modernisation.

detail.abstract: Organizations may experience productivity improvements from artificial intelligence without corresponding increases in enterprise value, as AI-driven productivity does not inherently lead to additional economic value. The Margin-Cap Trap occurs when AI enhances productive capacity without a strategic decision regarding its allocation. This article examines three strategies for utilizing released capacity: Labor Cost Optimization, Operational Workforce Augmentation, and Strategic Capacity Investment through Value-Based AI Arbitrage. An Enterprise AI Value Simulation assesses these strategies by modeling variations in workforce, workload demand, operating costs, operating profit, and enterprise value under different business scenarios. Under the modeled conditions, Strategic Capacity Investment through Value-Based AI Arbitrage yields the highest enterprise value by converting released capacity into additional value-generating demand in areas such as innovation, market expansion, and customer value. This framework offers a systematic approach for assessing AI-enabled capacity-allocation decisions and their financial implications.

detail.abstract: This paper formalizes the price and distribution dynamics of the generative artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem within the analytical framework of Piero Sraffa's Production of Commodities by Means of Commodities. By mapping the global AI supply chain-advanced semiconductor materials, pure-play foundries, GPU design, hyperscale cloud infrastructure, and frontier foundation models-into a linear inter-industry system, we model the recursive feedback wherein AI models and computational power are reinvested as intermediate inputs into semiconductor architecture design, lithographic yield optimization, and materials discovery. We prove mathematically that this feedback induces an endogenous topological phase transition: the system shifts from a decomposable (reducible) structure to an indecomposable (irreducible) one, establishing frontier AI compute as a classical Basic Commodity. Furthermore, we introduce asymmetric, sector-specific markups reflecting non-reproducible monopolistic bottlenecks (e.g., TSMC's advanced packaging and Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem). We demonstrate that upstream rent extraction contracts the global wage-profit frontier, pre-emptively absorbs the surplus of downstream model developers, and counteracts the deflationary pressures of algorithmic self-improvement. Finally, we discuss the vulnerability of massive capital expenditures (CAPEX) to the reswitching of techniques and propose a structural shift in antitrust policy from downstream consumer welfare to upstream input choke-points.

detail.abstract: This study examines the India-Japan Semiconductor Partnership as a strategic response to India's critical dependency on Chinese semiconductor imports. With China supplying 70-75 percent of India's computer imports and contributing to an $87.48 billion trade deficit in 2022, India faces acute economic, strategic, and technological vulnerabilities requiring urgent diversification. The partnership, formalized through a July 2023 Memorandum of Cooperation, combines Japan's semiconductor manufacturing expertise with India's large domestic market through institutional mechanisms including JBIC financing, IJICP industrial corridors, and technology transfer initiatives. Employing qualitative case study methodology with comparative analysis, this research examines the partnership's strategic rationale, institutional architecture, implementation challenges, and potential outcomes. Findings reveal sophisticated institutional design addressing financial support, infrastructure development, and workforce development simultaneously. However, formidable challenges emerge: capital requirements exceeding tens of billions, workforce skill gaps requiring 5-10 years to remedy, paradoxical dependence on Chinese rare earth materials, and infrastructure deficits. Unlike US partnerships with Taiwan and South Korea leveraging existing manufacturing excellence, India-Japan must build capabilities from scratch. The partnership represents a critical test case for bilateral cooperation as pathway to technological sovereignty in emerging economies, with implications for Indo-Pacific supply chain resilience and friendshoring viability in critical technology sectors.

detail.abstract: Behavioral assessment predicts individual workplace behavior, but weakly and conditionally: personality explains a small share of performance variance and only where the situation leaves room for it. This paper asks whether prediction survives the move to higher levels: from the individual to the human team, to the team that includes artificial-intelligence colleagues, to the firm in one country, and to the firm operating across several. It argues that each transition introduces a distinct translation problem (emergence, trust calibration, structure and leadership, cultural moderation, ecosystem fit) and specifies the rule that governs each. To make the argument testable, it maps the framework onto a single fully measured evolutionary case, the medium ground finch of Daphne Major under drought, abundance, competitor arrival and hybridisation, and treats the arrival of AI in the workplace as a disturbance of the same structural kind; the breeder's equation is proposed as a first-order estimator of organisational response. The framework is then set against nine countries in which the author held senior management roles, using a structured questionnaire and the author's own assessment profile as a disclosed instrument. At the human-AI level the paper contributes original data: a DISC-format instrument, a Big Five inventory and a repeated-game battery administered to AI colleagues configured as real corporate functions configure them, across four model versions from two providers (8,960 measurement units). The function that configures the colleague explains 65 to 92 per cent of the variance in its measured style and the model behind it less than 10 per cent, while behavior under provocation belongs to the model family and shifts with version updates the questionnaire cannot see. Thirteen propositions follow, two now carrying measurements. Two field findings are new: the role assigned to an advisor, human or artificial, tracks the organisation's decision latency rather than its national culture; and predictability depends less on how strong a situation is than on whether the source of its strength is codified.

detail.abstract: Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in public administration presents significant opportunities to enhance bureaucratic efficiency and public service delivery. This study examined the relationship of AI-driven documentation system on the administrative performance of employees in a selected Local Government Unit (LGU) in MIMAROPA Region, Philippines. Guided by the Task-Technology Fit Theory, this study employed a descriptive correlational research design to examine how AI-driven documentation system affects administrative performance among the 204 regular LGU employees. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire and responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Spearman's rankorder correlation to determine the relationship between the variables employed in the study. The study revealed that AIdriven documentation system in the subject LGU enhances processing speed, output quality, and record consistency leading to improved efficiency in administrative performance among employees. This confirms that AI-driven documentation system is significantly related to administrative performance. However, implementation of the AI-driven system remains constrained by technical, organizational, and human-related barriers, including system inconsistencies, output errors, limited training, security risks, and resistance to change. Relative to these findings, the researchers proposed an action plan to effectively utilize AI-driven documentation system for the administrative operations and services of the LGU. This study advances the understanding of technology-driven governance and supports broader digital transformation initiatives in local government operations.

detail.title:
The Upstream Border

Artificial Intelligence and the Unbundling of Economic Sovereignty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: se;f

detail.abstract:
International trade law and economic sovereignty developed around a physical convention: economically valuable transactions became legible when goods crossed territorial borders. Artificial intelligence weakens this convention by separating technical quantity, commercial value, compute location, technology ownership, physical resource use, customer location, and rent capture. This paper develops a conceptual framework for what is termed the upstream border: the migration of sovereign leverage away from the final digital output and toward the physical, legal, and institutional layers required to produce it.

The paper advances six related propositions. First, Japan retains disproportionate leverage in selected semiconductor materials and equipment despite limited ownership of frontier AI models. Second, the July 2023 tightening of Japanese semiconductor-equipment export controls is associated with a compositional shift in exports to China toward mature-node and uncontrolled tools. Third, AI scale-up makes electricity, cooling water, grid connections, and land increasingly binding location constraints. Fourth, generative AI converts apparently intangible computation into a thermodynamic infrastructure problem. Fifth, low-cost power jurisdictions in Central Asia can become compute enclaves, but headline investment need not translate into commensurate domestic value capture. Sixth, AI-era state power is functionally distributed across model architecture, fabrication, upstream inputs, regulation, energy hosting, and market access rather than concentrated in a single sovereign stack.

The empirical material is comparative and illustrative rather than causal. Cases include Thailand, Japan, the United States, China, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Taiwan, the Netherlands, and South Korea. The central claim is not that borders disappear. Rather, the final AI output becomes less territorially legible while strategic control migrates upstream to semiconductor inputs, fabrication capacity, grid access, energy, land, taxation, licensing, regulation, and social license. Economic sovereignty therefore becomes distributed, overlapping, and increasingly dependent on asymmetric substitutability and switching time.

title: Why Real Estate and Labubu Can Predict DRAMs Boom-to-Bust Cycle: A Theory of Decision Time Asymmetry and Loss Aversion Amplification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest related to this research.

detail.abstract: Why do real estate, collectible toys (Labubu), and semiconductor memory (DRAM) exhibit nearly identical price dynamics—sharp booms, prolonged stagnation, and sudden busts—despite having different fundamentals, participant groups, and institutional settings? And why does observing the boom‑bust sequence in one market allow us to predict the same sequence in the others? This paper proposes a unified theoretical framework based on a single structural variable: the fundamental asymmetry between purchase decision time and sale decision time (Tin << Tout). When market participants can complete a purchase in seconds but require weeks, months, or years to complete a sale, the market becomes structurally unstable. This asymmetry temporally amplifies loss aversion (Leff = α * Tout), suppresses sale decisions, locks effective supply, and makes price signals dependent on expectations rather than fundamentals. Under positive expectations, this structure generates self‑reinforcing booms; under negative expectations, it generates self‑reinforcing busts. The key predictive contribution is that markets sharing this structural condition are predictively equivalent: real estate, Labubu, and DRAM differ only in scale—price scale, time scale, participant scale—but their underlying dynamics are identical. Real estate, with the longest selling time, displays the full sequence first and serves as the slowest leading indicator; Labubu displays it fastest; DRAM follows with timing proportional to its selling time. The theory yields a specific, testable prediction: once DRAM expectations turn negative, prices will inevitably crash, following a stagnation‑then‑collapse pattern. Equities, where Tin ≈ Tout, serve as the counterexample that validates the theory.

detail.abstract: A companion study found that on individual stocks the two most common moving average timing signals-price relative to the average, and the direction (slope) of the average-behave differently: the slope rule earns more but draws down deeper, because a smoothed average turns late while a price cross exits fast. This paper asks whether that distinction survives, and can be exploited, when the signals are applied Faber-style to a diversified asset-class basket, each sleeve timed independently with cash held in Treasury bills. On recent ETF baskets (2007-2026) the two signals are a near-wash and no rule beats buy-and-hold on return-timing is purely a drawdown-reduction dial. On a long-history US multi-asset basket (1988-2026), however, the slope rule clearly pulls ahead: it keeps 94% of buy-and-hold's return (7.7% vs 8.2%) at a third of the drawdown (-10% vs-29%), out-Sharpes the price-cross rule 1.20 vs 1.09, and the timing rules trace a smooth, tunable return/drawdown frontier on which the price cross and a naive blend are dominated. The slope advantage is robust to basket composition (it strengthens when bonds are removed, ruling out a bond-bull artifact) and to transaction costs, and holds in three of four decades, failing only in the sharp-reversal 2020s-but it is bounded to conventional average lengths (10-12 months); at 6-8 months the ranking inverts. We conclude that the choice of trend signal is a responsiveness decision matched to the regime, not an alpha ranking: slope for long smooth trends, price cross for sharp reversals, with a graded combination available as a middle point.

detail.abstract: The United States roadway network — comprising approximately 4.2 million miles of public roads supporting more than 297 million registered vehicles — faces a structural maintenance crisis characterized by an accumulated backlog of approximately $1 trillion in road and bridge repairs and a road condition rating of D+ (ASCE, 2025). The dominant reactive maintenance paradigm generates lifecycle costs 4–7 times higher than preventive intervention, imposes an estimated $169 billion annually in additional vehicle operating costs on U.S. drivers, and coincides with 39,254 traffic fatalities in 2024, with inadequate roadway safety features identified as a contributing factor in approximately one-third of fatal crashes. This paper proposes the design and implementation of an Intelligent Digital Monitoring System (IDMS) for roadway infrastructure, integrating embedded IoT sensor networks, machine learning-based predictive analytics, and real-time geospatial dashboards tailored for U.S. state Departments of Transportation. Field-calibrated algorithms developed under this initiative demonstrate predictive accuracy of approximately 85% in identifying maintenance intervention windows, with projected cost reductions of 20–25% in the short term (0–24 months) and 35–40% at full deployment maturity (36–60 months), as the system accumulates operational data and algorithmic precision improves. The proposed framework addresses a critical gap in national infrastructure asset management, with direct implications for public safety, economic competitiveness, and the United States' strategic positioning in intelligent infrastructure technology. Implementation across ten states and 1,000 monitored miles is projected to generate $95–$165 million in cumulative net economic benefit over five years and support 40–55 U.S. jobs. The intellectual property underlying this system is protected under USPTO Provisional Patent Application No. 64/116,669, filed July 21, 2026.

detail.title: Spillover Effects of Regulatory Inspections: Evidence from OSHA
detail.abstract:
Regulatory inspections might affect entities nearby those inspected. Such spillovers are difficult to identify because regulators target inspections and neighboring establishments face correlated shocks. We exploit the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration’s Site-Specific Targeting (SST) program, which generated quasi-random variation in inspections among workplaces with injury rates near a discrete cutoff. An SST inspection reduced injuries at uninspected same-ZIP-code establishments by an estimated 11 percent—an effect roughly as large as the direct effect on the inspected establishment. Because spillovers extend to multiple nearby establishments, they avert several times as many injuries as the inspection’s direct effect.

detail.abstract:
Context. Aerospace supplier qualification packages sit inside a mature standards architecture. AS9102 Rev C prescribes the content and form of the First Article Inspection Report. AS9145 establishes the aerospace Advanced Product Quality Planning and Production Part Approval Process framework. AS9103 Rev B governs variation management of key characteristics, and clause 8.7 of AS9100 Rev D governs control of nonconforming outputs. No standards body, original equipment manufacturer or peer-reviewed source publishes a rejection-rate benchmark for these submissions.
Objective. To record what experienced quality personnel say they examine first when a supplier qualification package arrives, and to state a falsifiable hypothesis about the conditions under which such packages are returned.
Methodology. I conducted non-probability convenience sampling through professional network outreach between May and September 2026. I identified 642 individuals and contacted 311. Twenty-three substantive responses were recorded. Nine addressed submission failure and eight answered the question as posed. Five participants gave written consent for attribution and appear here under role descriptors.
Findings. The accounts describe inconsistency between constituent documents, and customer expectations that were never written down, rather than absent documents. A participant follow-up separates a second condition, in which the AS9102 forms are complete but supporting objective evidence required by the specification, the special process or the regulatory context was never established as applicable. One participant reported that the condition does not arise inside an established quality management system.
Practical Implications. The reported failure mode is provisionally tied to a supplier's first submission to a new customer. I specify a structured verification study and the results that would falsify the hypothesis.

detail.abstract: Stan Weinstein's four-stage analysis (basing, advancing, topping, declining), organized around the 30-week moving average, is among the most widely taught frameworks in technical analysis, yet it has never been formally tested as a taxonomy. Its components-moving-average trend filters, relative strength, and time-series momentum-are individually well studied, but the stage classification itself has not been isolated. We mechanize the four stages as a faithful state machine and note that its distinctive content reduces to a single, testable proposition: because a flat 30-week moving average characterizes both Stage 1 (basing) and Stage 3 (topping), and a trend filter cannot tell them apart, all of the taxonomy's incremental information lives in whether the basing/topping distinction predicts returns. On 901,533 survivorship-free stock-weeks of point-in-time S&P 500 membership (1992-2026), using Fama-MacBeth regressions with Newey-West standard errors, we find it does not: among flat-moving-average weeks, basing weeks do not out-earn topping weeks (13-week difference-0.6%/yr, t =-0.5), a null robust across twelve classifier specifications. Only Stage 2 earns a positive market-excess return (+2.3%/yr, t = 2.7)-but Stage 2 is, by construction, a rising moving-average trend filter. A nested portfolio test confirms the economic version: a "full Weinstein" book that trades the stage memory is statistically and visually identical to a one-line moving-average filter (Sharpe 0.85 vs 0.85; MAR 0.32 vs 0.32). Finally, we quantify why practitioner backtests mislead: applying today's index members backward inflates the Stage-2 return by 6.3%/yr. We conclude that Weinstein's Stage 2 works because it is a moving-average trend filter, and that the taxonomy's distinctive apparatus-the basing/topping memory and the relative-strength overlay-is empirically inert for forecasting returns.

detail.abstract: This treatise proposes and defines the foundational conceptual frameworks of "AI Transcendentalism" (AI 超验主义, or AI 超验) and "Silicon Transcendentalism" (硅基超验主义, or 硅基超验), establishing the technical-philosophical boundaries between computational state representation and biological intervention. As large language models and autonomous agents assume an expanding share of decision-making in pharmaceutical research, modern R&D operates under an implicit technological faith: that continuous architectural scaling and tokenized biological data will automatically yield causal discoveries. Writing from Walden Pond, the historical center of New England Transcendentalism, the author argues that this ideology conflates state classification with dynamic transformation. Observational datasets (such as static single-cell transcriptomic profiles) teach a model the static "nouns" (cellular states) of biology, but fail to inherently resolve the transactional "verbs" (directional perturbations) that govern therapeutic outcomes. No amount of computational scaling substitutes for anchoring algorithmic hypotheses within complementary multi-modal matrices and empirical wet-lab validation. The essay extends this inquiry to clinical outcome prediction, where increasingly accurate forecasts of longitudinal disease trajectories and mortality risk remain safe only as long as an accurate forecast is not mistaken for a validated treatment-selection rule, and where even a correctly used forecast trades human narrative contingency for statistical certainty. The treatise concludes by outlining an Emersonian middle path of evidence-anchored technological practice, positioning Silicon Transcendentalism as a distinct modern philosophical inquiry into the boundaries of human and machine intelligence.

detail.abstract: Do policymakers listen to stock markets when deciding which industries lose key policy support? We examine this question in the context of China's industrial policy dismantling across the 12th, 13th, and 14th Five-Year Plans (2011–2021). Dismantling refers to removing or downgrading an industry from key supported status. We identify dismantling by translating expert reading and keyword-matching procedures into structured large language model (LLM) prompts that rely on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Using probit models, we link pre-decision stock returns to the probability of dismantling. Industries with lower past cumulative returns (PastCR) during the information-gathering stage of policy drafting are significantly more likely to lose key support. This effect is stronger where public information is scarce, as in industries with limited media coverage and highly similar annual reports. These results are consistent with the view that stock prices convey complementary information rather than merely reflect common fundamentals. A Karlson–Holm–Breen decomposition attributes approximately one-tenth of the total effect to a reassessment of industry innovation capacity. Our results extend the price-informativeness literature to the policy domain. The proposed LLM-based approach provides a reproducible pipeline for extracting industry-level policy variables.

detail.abstract:
Background: Evidence from African small island developing states on how reported COVID-19 transmission and severe outcomes evolved across successive pandemic years remains limited. We aimed to analyse the temporal evolution of incidence, mortality, and case fatality in Cabo Verde from 2020 to 2023 and quantify inter-annual differences in reported epidemiological risk.

Methods: We conducted a nationwide ecological time-series study using daily COVID-19 surveillance data aggregated by calendar month and year. Monthly case and death counts were analysed with negative binomial regression using log population as an offset; case fatality was analysed with quasibinomial regression using deaths and survivors among confirmed cases. Overall monthly incidence trend was assessed with log-linear regression and 10 000 bootstrap resamples.

Findings: Between 2020 and 2023, Cabo Verde reported 64,474 confirmed COVID-19 cases and 417 deaths. Annual incidence increased from 1,972.14 per 100,000 in 2020 to 4,604.98 in 2021, remained high in 2022 (4,075.95), and declined to 216.47 in 2023. Compared with 2020, incidence was lower in 2023 (IRR 0.11, 95% CI 0.03–0.36; p=0.0003), as was mortality (MRR 0.04, 0.01–0.19; p<0.0001). Case-fatality odds were lower in 2022 (OR 0.26, 0.15–0.45; p<0.0001), but not in 2023 (OR 0.40, 0.08–1.98; p=0.2708). The monthly incidence trend was −4.58% (95% bootstrap CI −11.22 to 2.41; p=0.1876), providing no evidence of a global log-linear trend.

Interpretation:  Reported COVID-19 indicators in Cabo Verde followed non-parallel trajectories across 2020–2023. Case-fatality odds were lower in 2022, whereas model-based reductions in incidence and mortality relative to 2020 were clearly evident in 2023. The absence of a significant global log-linear incidence trend reflects the strongly non-linear sequence of epidemic waves and subsequent decline.

detail.abstract: AI tech giants are planning to harvest their "data farms" on America's fields, as demand for hyperscale data centers is predicted to triple by 2030. These water guzzling, energy hogs often exceed 10,000 square feet and are transforming rural land into industrial zones. This Article argues that municipal environmental sovereignty is imperative when emerging technology expands to areas never intended for industrial use. The Trump Administration has pledged to Make America the AI Capital of the World. Consistent with this pledge, and sweeping federal deregulation, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has announced it has no plans to implement nationwide environmental regulations for data centers. Regulation rests in the hands of state and local governments. As farmland continues to shrink and as millennials and GenZs migrate to rural communities, opposition to data center development has become an increasingly vocal matter of public concern. The infrastructure required to support data centers is draining resources and impacting water quality, air quality, biodiversity and the cultural identity of many communities. Euclid zoning rests on the foundational principle that municipalities may exercise their police power to protect public health, safety, and general welfare. This Article provides a comparative analysis of moratoriums, bans, conditional-use permitting, and other zoning tools as local governments attempt to regulate this new land use within the scope of state enabling statutes, the limits of federal and state preemption, and logistical constraints.

detail.abstract: Financial knowledge is often treated as a pathway to better financial outcomes, yet economically underserved young adults may face resource constraints that limit their ability to convert knowledge into action. This study examines the association between financial knowledge and five financial behaviors among U.S. adults ages 18 to 24, using the 2018 and 2021 National Financial Capability Study (NFCS) as the primary inferential data source. Because the surveys record income differently, lower-income status is defined per source: in the NFCS-the inferential core, which reports income only in bands and does not collect household size-as household income below $35,000 per year, and in the descriptive-tier surveys (SCF, CFPB, and NLSY97) as household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Survey-weighted logistic regressions estimate associations with maintaining an emergency fund, paying credit-card balances in full, overspending, carrying an interest-bearing balance, and overdrawing a checking account, with credit-card and checking-account outcomes restricted to applicable respondents. Three additional national surveys-the Survey of Consumer Finances, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau data, and the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997-provide limited, direction-only corroboration rather than directly comparable replication evidence, and the evidence across them is mixed. In the NFCS, estimated knowledge-behavior associations were more consistently distinguishable from zero in 2018 than in 2021, particularly within the underserved sample. However, differences in within-wave statistical significance do not by themselves establish that the underlying associations changed between waves. The findings therefore support a limited conclusion: financial knowledge is associated with some beneficial behaviors, but the strength and detectability of those associations vary across behaviors, samples, and periods. Because the data are observational, cross-sectional within wave, and based partly on self-reported behavior, the results neither identify the causal effect of financial education nor establish a COVID-19 mechanism. Financial knowledge is best understood as one input into financial behavior whose practical value may depend on the resources and opportunities available to act on it.

detail.abstract: Adolescence represents a critical developmental stage characterized by significant physiological transitions and the formation of self-identity and social bonds. This study investigated the extent to which social media usage patterns predict adolescents' self-identity, social relationships, and perceptions of societal expectations. Data analysis utilized descriptive statistics, normality testing (Skewness and Kurtosis), and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) models to isolate the predictive power of passive versus active digital behaviors. Descriptive findings indicated a "Moderate Influence" across all three domains: self-identity (M = 3.13), social relationships (M = 3.30), and societal perceptions (M = 3.16). While usage duration was diverse, MLR models identified a definitive "Quality-Quantity Paradox." Cumulative usage duration (Hours) was found to be a non-significant predictor in all models (all p > .40). However, Posting Frequency emerged as a significant positive predictor for Self-Identity (B = 0.134, p = 0.006), Social Relationships (B = 0.129, p = 0.007), and Societal Expectations (B = 0.131, p = 0.003). The models explained between 5.3% and 6.1\% of the variance, reaching overall statistical significance (all p < .05). The study reveals that for rural Filipino adolescents, psychosocial development is driven by active digital agency rather than mere exposure time.

title: The profit-bias identity in sports betting: bookmaker profit as the public's prediction error

detail.title: The profit-bias identity in sports betting: bookmaker profit as the public's prediction error

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to influence the study.

detail.abstract: Sports betting moves money continuously from a large public to a small number of firms. The most influential account of that flow, due to Levitt (2004), holds that books price away from the market-clearing point to exploit predictable public biases. It computes profit from two numbers (the probability that a side wins the proposition and the fraction of handle it attracts), treating the share on a side as independent of the outcome. Here we relax that assumption and derive a profit-bias identity: profit is affine and increasing in the expected share of handle on the losing side, with Levitt's expression as the special case of independence. The identity resolves the book's margin into exactly three channels: its hold, the product of its price shading and the public's lean, and the covariance between bet share and outcome. A lean is thus worthless without shading, and shading is worthless without a lean. Under a public-belief model, the profit driver is the public's Bayes error: the probability of a representative bettor selecting the losing side. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a "Goldilocks Zone": prices at which book and bettor both profit. Testing these predictions on 1,139 Major League Baseball games, we find that the apparent dependence between bet share and outcome is a Simpson's paradox: present when games are pooled, but absent once they are separated by which side the book favored. The public leans heavily toward favorites, but we detect no matching shading, and the realized margin is indistinguishable from the hold.
