declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit organization.

detail.abstract:
This study adopts an econometric approach to examine the determinants of agricultural production in Ketugram-I Block, West Bengal. Using primary cross-sectional survey data, an agricultural production function is estimated with total crop output as the dependent variable and cultivated land, irrigation, labor, soil quality, farming experience, and other farm-specific characteristics as explanatory variables.
The production function is estimated using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), followed by diagnostic tests for multicollinearity and heteroscedasticity to assess the validity of the model. The estimated coefficients are interpreted to evaluate the contribution of each input to agricultural output and to derive evidence-based policy implications. As the analysis uses cross-sectional data, tests for autocorrelation are not applicable.
The remainder of this dissertation is organized as follows: Section 2 reviews the relevant literature, Section 3 outlines the research objectives, Section 4 describes the data and methodology, Section 5 presents the regression analysis, Sections 6 and 7 discuss the diagnostic tests and remedial estimation, and Sections 8 and 9 present the policy implications and conclusion.

title: The Event Clock: Identifying Physical Information from State Prices
affiliations: , , University of Liechtenstein and

detail.title: The Event Clock: Identifying Physical Information from State Prices

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: State-price recovery asks when prices identify physical probabilities. We show that even when probability levels are not recoverable, state-price dynamics can identify economically meaningful features of physical learning. With three economically distinct pricing systems, cross-system residual orthogonality identifies each system's learning-spanned component and variance share without normalizing loadings. Bounded residual correlation yields sharp sensitivity sets, while an economic anchor is required only to express the common component on the physical Event Clock scale; without one, that scale is globally nonidentified. In 2024 U.S. presidential-election data, Polymarket, Kalshi, and Betfair place 75% of national cross-venue covariance variation by November 4 and 90% by November 5. Sampling-frequency-corrected shares are economically substantial but assumption-sensitive. A panel of seven battleground-state markets reproduces the same late milestones, which survive every leave-one-state-out exercise. Generic pre-resolution risk-premium restrictions cannot supply the state-conditional valuation bound needed to recover the physical clock from one pricing system.

title: MR-CaPER: A multimodal residual calibration and prediction-error ranking architecture for multi-label chest radiograph classification
affiliations: Shandong University of Science and Technology, Shandong University of Science and Technology and Shandong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: MR-CaPER: A multimodal residual calibration and prediction-error ranking architecture for multi-label chest radiograph classification
detail.abstract: Background and Objectives:Deep learning has significantly advanced multi-label chest radiograph classification, but existing studies have focused mainly on discrimination metrics such as the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), with less attention to probability calibration and the ranking of error-prone images. High discrimination does not necessarily ensure well-calibrated disease probabilities or effective error prioritisation. We propose Multimodal Residual Calibration and Prediction-Error Ranking(MR-CaPER) to improve disease-probability quality and image-level prediction-error ranking while preserving the discrimination of the original visual classifier.Methods:On the public NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset, a patient-level out-of-fold (OOF) procedure generated spatial visual features and 14 disease scores for fusion-model training, ensuring that each patient's features were extracted by a classifier not trained on that patient. MR-CaPER combined these inputs with age, sex, and projection-view metadata as projected multisource tokens. A DeepSeek backbone adapted using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) produced bounded logit residuals and an image-level prediction-error score. The original classifier, logit-only vector scaling, and three MR-CaPER implementations—Transformer, frozen-parameter DeepSeek, and DeepSeek-LoRA—were evaluated on a locked internal test set of 25,596 images from 2,797 patients; learned methods used three fixed seeds, and patient-level paired bootstrapping quantified uncertainty. The primary endpoint was macro Brier score; macro expected calibration error (ECE) and the area under the risk–coverage curve (AURC) were secondary endpoints. Lower macro Brier score and ECE indicate smaller probability errors, whereas lower AURC indicates better error ranking.Results:Compared with the original uncalibrated visual classifier, MR-CaPER reduced macro Brier score, macro ECE, and AURC by 28.84%, 85.74%, and 25.87%, respectively, while essentially preserving macro AUROC. All three MR-CaPER implementations produced closely grouped macro Brier scores (0.057312–0.057342), macro ECE values (0.013259–0.013982), and AURCs (0.037311–0.038479), all numerically lower than the corresponding values for vector scaling (0.069992, 0.055399, and 0.043527, respectively). The closely grouped fusion-model results indicate that the gains were robust to backbone choice, with DeepSeek-LoRA attaining the lowest numerical AURC.Conclusions:MR-CaPER improved disease-probability quality and prediction-error ranking while essentially preserving discrimination. This study provides a novel methodological contribution to the field of intelligent medicine, enhancing the reliability of AI-assisted diagnosis and treatment.

title: Active Scientific Knowledge: A Conceptual Model for Machine-Actionable and Versioned Science
affiliations: Anadolu University

detail.title: Active Scientific Knowledge: A Conceptual Model for Machine-Actionable and Versioned Science

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: Science has digitized its documents without fully representing the knowledge relations they contain. Claims, evidence, methods, provenance, scope conditions, and revision histories remain dispersed across files and repositories. This article proposes the Active Scientific Knowledge (ASK) model as a conceptual framework for scientific entities that can participate in subsequent inquiry without losing the conditions that warrant their use. ASK defines activation across six related capacities: semantic addressability, evidential traceability, conditional executability, responsiveness to new evidence, context-preserving transferability, and contestable federation. It builds on Semantic Web technologies, nanopublications, research objects, FAIR Digital Objects, executable workflows, and living evidence systems, but extends them by treating a versioned epistemic state and scopepreserving operational reuse as joint requirements. AlphaFold databases, automated laboratories, and scientific agents illustrate a broader transition in which scientific outputs increasingly serve as inputs to prediction, hypothesis generation, analysis, and experimentation. These developments also expose a structural weakness: systems may recover conclusions from prose while losing their evidential and contextual limits. ASK therefore provides a five-stage roadmap from documentbound publication to structured, semantic, executable, and active scientific entities. The model does not delegate scientific judgment to algorithms. It makes repeatable checks, interpretive decisions, and changes in epistemic status traceable. The transition toward machine-actionable scientific knowledge is already underway; its institutional form remains a choice between transparent, federated infrastructures and opaque proprietary reconstruction.

title: Does Explainability Improve False-Alarm Triage in ECG Monitoring? A Pre-Registered, Budget-Matched Evaluation on MIT-BIH and PTB-XL
affiliations: Macquarie University and Daffodil International University

detail.title: Does Explainability Improve False-Alarm Triage in ECG Monitoring? A Pre-Registered, Budget-Matched Evaluation on MIT-BIH and PTB-XL

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Explanation-derived features have been proposed as a lightweight, on-device signal for suppressing false alarms in continuous ECG monitoring, but whether this promise survives a held-out test set and a simple baseline has not been established under a pre-registered protocol. We built XFAD, a two-stage false-alarm gate driven by Grad-CAM saliency, signal-quality, and confidence features computed for every alarm raised by a compact multi-task student distilled from two specialist teachers (a beat-morphology 1D-CNN on MIT-BIH; a rhythm 1D-ResNet on PTB-XL). Gate thresholds were calibrated once, on five inter-patient validation records, under a pre-registered 2% sensitivityloss budget, and evaluated once on the untouched MIT-BIH DS2 test partition (2,850 student alarm events from 21 DS2 records with at least one alarm). The distilled student attains higher raw accuracy than its teachers on both datasets (87.4% vs 78.2% on MIT-BIH; 67.5% vs 60.5% on PTB-XL; McNemar p<0.001 both), but this is driven by the dominant normal class: macro-F1 (25.7% vs 36.2%; 16.7% vs 42.5%) and abnormal recall (20.1% vs 58.9%; 32.1% vs 90.6%) are both substantially lower, and abnormal-vs-normal AUROC favours the teachers on both datasets (DeLong p<0.001). On validation, the calibrated gate met its pre-registered budget (18.6% false-alarm reduction at 1.78% sensitivity loss). On the held-out test set, no policy met the budget: the full two-stage gate achieved the largest reduction among explainability-guided policies (30.7%, 95% CI 17.0-49.8%, at 13.6% sensitivity loss), but a budgetmatched signal-quality-index baseline was statistically indistinguishable and numerically higher (33.2%, 12.3% loss). A saliency-matching distillation ablation improved macro-F1 and abnormal recall but cut test-set false-alarm suppression to 8.3%, confounded by a roughly four-fold rise in alarm volume. We conclude that explanation-derived triage is feasible and suppresses a meaningful fraction of false alarms on unseen data, but does not outperform a simple, equally budget-matched SQI rule, and the sensitivity constraint that held on validation does not transfer to test. Aligning student and teacher attention degraded gate performance. We report this as a negative result and outline conditions, a persistence-aware alarm definition, evaluation against PhysioNet/CinC 2015, and larger calibration cohorts, for retesting the hypothesis.

title: Artificial Intelligence, specialized assets and corporate diversification
affiliations: University of Wollongong and University of Wollongong

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, specialized assets and corporate diversification
detail.abstract: Drawing on the knowledge-based view, this study examines the impact of AI innovation on corporate diversification decisions. Using a sample of U.S.-listed firms from 2010 to 2022, we document that AI innovation leads to a significant reduction in corporate diversification, driving firms toward greater strategic focus. To establish causality, we exploit two exogenous shocks: the 2016 deep learning breakthrough and the staggered adoption of state-level AI legislation. Mechanism tests reveal that AI innovation reduces diversification incentives by enhancing asset specificity through specialized asset investment and human capital specificity. In addition, the main effect is more pronounced among firms with shorter cash conversion cycles, smaller size, lower AI intensity, and headquartered in non-high-tech states. Overall, our findings highlight AI innovation as a vital driver of corporate specialization and provide novel insight into how emerging technologies reshape corporate boundaries, investment decisions, and resource allocation.

title: Deep Learning Assisted Disposable Biosensing Platform for Reliable and Low-Cost ABO Blood Typing
affiliations: Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur, All India Institute of Medical Sciences Jodhpur and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Jodhpur

detail.title: Deep Learning Assisted Disposable Biosensing Platform for Reliable and Low-Cost ABO Blood Typing
detail.abstract: Accurate blood typing is paramount for safe transfusion practices and preventing life-threatening complications. However, existing diagnostic methods often suffer from limitations such as disposable issues, rapid reaction kinetics, low sensitivity, narrow dynamic ranges, and a lack of portability or low-power operation. This study presents the design and development of a biodegradable sensing strip for reliable and efficient ABO blood group identification. In this study, the sensing platform employs a vertical flow mechanism comprising different combinations of Whatman filter paper, achieving 84% accuracy with the grade 1-1 combination during visual inspection. The sensing platform, which uses a layered approach, includes several parameters: temperature (84% accuracy at 25-35°C), heat drying (92% accuracy at 20-30°C), and air drying (84% accuracy at 15°C), thereby enhancing overall sensing accuracy. Agglutination intensity was quantified by optical microscopy and ImageJ, yielding statistically significant discrimination between positive and negative results (t = 11.85 for group A, t = 13.11 for group B). Afterward, a convolutional neural network (CNN) was integrated into the system, achieving 87.5% accuracy in image-based classification. Moreover, a comparative analysis with standard tube tests across 40 clinical samples yielded 85% agreement and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.79, indicating substantial concordance. Biodegradability studies demonstrated a 32% reduction in substrate weight over 60 days, affirming the environmental sustainability of the sensing substrate. Therefore, the proposed concept offers a promising solution for accurate, efficient, and environmentally friendly blood group detection, with potential applications in clinical settings, blood banks, and research laboratories.

title: Multivariate Time-Series Analysis of Energy Futures: VAR, Cointegration and the Vector Error Correction Model
affiliations: AlgosWorks AI Ltd

detail.title: Multivariate Time-Series Analysis of Energy Futures: VAR, Cointegration and the Vector Error Correction Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Econometric analysis
declarations.funderStatement: Not funded

detail.abstract: This paper sets out a complete, reproducible framework for the multivariate analysis of cointegrated energy-futures prices, aimed at quantitative practitioners. Working with five major energy futurescrude oil, ethanol, gasoline, heating oil and natural gas-I move from univariate stationarity testing (Augmented Dickey-Fuller and KPSS) through vector autoregression on returns, to cointegration analysis and a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). I contrast the Engle-Granger two-step procedure with the Johansen maximum-likelihood approach, and argue that the latter is the appropriate tool for a system of more than two integrated series, both because it tests for multiple cointegrating relations and because it avoids the generated-regressor problem. The empirical illustration identifies a single cointegrating relation among the five series and recovers the corresponding adjustment dynamics. The emphasis is methodological: the contribution is a clear, honest and fully reproducible pipeline, not a claim of out-of-sample predictive power, whose limits for econometric models on daily data are discussed explicitly.

title: Cross-Border Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets: Evidence from the India-United States Corridor
affiliations: Deuterium Consultants (OPC) Private Limited and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Indore - Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Indore, Students

detail.title: Cross-Border Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets: Evidence from the India-United States Corridor

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. The research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors. Neither author has any commercial, contractual or advisory relationship with any of the exchanges whose data are analysed (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, CoinDCX, WazirX), and neither has received data, access or consideration from them; all exchange data were obtained from public interfaces.
declarations.funderStatement: The project is built on public datasets and ML and Python based on open-source software, so no funding was required.

detail.abstract: Cryptocurrency should be the easiest asset in which to enforce the law of one price: fungible, transferable within minutes, quoted continuously worldwide. Between India and the dollar market it is not. Across 2,942 date-matched asset-venue-day observations for Bitcoin, Ether and Tether on two Indian exchanges between July 2022 and June 2025, Indian prices stand 5.38% above dollar prices on average, higher on 97.18% of observations and equal on none. Correcting the standard errors for strong serial dependence roughly halves the t-statistics, to 19-22, and leaves the rejection undisturbed. Working in logs, so that the premium is a genuine linear combination of the two price series, the four volatile-asset panels behave as a cointegrated system: both legs non-stationary, the log premium stationary, and a freely estimated cointegrating vector within 2.2% of [1,-1]. Stationarity tests nonetheless reject a constant mean, and a unit-root test allowing one endogenous break rejects everywhere, so the premium reverts around a level that shifts rather than converging to parity. A stablecoin panel, whose dollar leg is a peg, fails these procedures as the theory predicts and serves as a negative control. How much is executable is a weaker claim. High-frequency records from one Indian venue over roughly 2.8 days show a quoted spread averaging 48.19 basis points and resting depth of about 0.24 BTC on the offer against 0.11 BTC on the bid. Under a squareroot price-impact law we prove that an optimising arbitrageur retains exactly one third of the cost-adjusted premium, whatever the venue's volume and whatever the impact coefficient; that share is the only parameter-free result in the exercise. A calibration whose cost and compliance inputs are assumed leaves about 0.6 percentage points per cycle, and the impact coefficient that would locate the viability boundary is not estimated. What survives is a ranking-the deeper stablecoin rail tolerates roughly twice the impact coefficient of the Bitcoin rail-and a mechanism: capturable size scales with venue depth, so the liquidity that would make the trade worth running is the liquidity whose arrival would compete the premium away.

title: Energy Policies and Green Economic Growth in the Regions of Indonesia Since 2015: A Comprehensive Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Energy Policies and Green Economic Growth in the Regions of Indonesia Since 2015: A Comprehensive Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding from any funding agency, commercial entity, or not-for-profit organization.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between energy policies and green economic growth across the diverse regions of Indonesia over the period 2015 to 2024. Indonesia, the largest economy in Southeast Asia and the world's sixth-largest greenhouse gas emitter, has introduced a range of energy policies aimed at increasing renewable energy adoption, improving energy efficiency, and reducing fossil-fuel dependence. Drawing on panel data from six major island groups-Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Bali and Nusa Tenggara, and Maluku and Papua-the study employs a fixed-effects regression model with mediation analysis to test five hypotheses linking energy policy instruments to green economic growth through the mechanism of energy transition. The findings indicate that renewable energy policies have a statistically significant positive association with green economic growth (β = 0.342, p < 0.01), while energy-efficiency policies (β = 0.218, p < 0.01) and fossil-fuel reduction measures (β = 0.287, p < 0.01) also demonstrate positive effects. Crucially, the energy transition variable mediates approximately 41.2% of the total policy effect. The analysis further reveals that regional heterogeneity significantly moderates these relationships, with regions possessing greater renewable energy potential, stronger infrastructure, and higher levels of institutional capacity benefiting more from energy policy interventions. The paper contributes to the growing literature on green growth in developing economies by demonstrating that the effectiveness of energy policies is contingent on regional characteristics and the pace of structural energy transition.

detail.abstract: With a global population surpassing 7.8 billion, promoting sustainable economic growth and good employment opportunities is a major global priority. This study focuses on the fundamental aspects of decent work, exploring its core pillars and their variations across developing economies. By examining the relationship between decent work and some selected variables such as gender equality, foreign investment, child labor, and the informal sector, this research sheds light on the problems related to labor conditions. Drawing insights from regions like South Korea, South Africa, and some selected Arab countries, the study not only contributes to academic discourse but also provides guidance for policymakers and practitioners aiming to enhance working conditions and proposing future research directions with the focus on some selected Arab countries.

title: The Dependency Premium: How Export Concentration Increases Sovereign Borrowing Costs and Sovereign Risk in Commodity-Dependent Economies

detail.title: The Dependency Premium: How Export Concentration Increases Sovereign Borrowing Costs and Sovereign Risk in Commodity-Dependent Economies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial or personal relationships with individuals or organizations that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, the research, analysis, interpretation, or conclusions presented in this paper. The paper forms part of the author’s independent research programme on Execution Economics, developed through VitroScript. VitroScript is the author’s research and consulting platform; however, no client, funder, government agency, private organization, or other external party provided financial support for this research or exercised influence over its content or conclusions.

The research, analysis, and preparation of the manuscript were undertaken by the author under the Execution Economics research programme developed through VitroScript.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Dependency Premium as a conceptual doctrine within the Execution Economics Canon. It proposes that an economy whose export base or fiscal revenue is concentrated in a limited number of commodities or revenue sources may face an additional structural financing cost because concentration increases exposure to external price, demand, and foreign-exchange shocks. The paper does not argue that markets irrationally misprice concentration risk. Rather, it proposes that concentration-related exposure can constitute a distinct component of financing cost that may be more visible in market-priced sovereign debt than in an economy's blended average borrowing cost. The proposition is positioned against an established empirical literature showing that commodity prices, terms-of-trade volatility, commodity dependence, and institutional conditions affect sovereign risk and external debt outcomes. The contribution of this paper is therefore not to establish the commodity sovereign risk relationship itself, but to develop a diagnostic framework for examining how concentration-related risk may appear differently across segments of a sovereign financing portfolio. The paper applies this framework to a documented African financing pattern in which sovereign bond spreads have declined while African issuers continue to face a measurable borrowing-cost differential relative to similarly rated peers. It then illustrates the segment-visibility problem through Cameroon, where a credit rating identifies sensitivity to export-revenue shocks as a structural risk while the country's reported blended average borrowing cost has declined. The case is treated as illustrative rather than causal. The paper proposes three provisional indicators: export concentration, the market-versus-blended financing-cost gap, and concentration-related language in sovereign credit assessments. Four falsifiable hypotheses are developed, including a proposed relationship between export diversification, domestic value addition, and the market-versus-blended financing-cost gap. The paper concludes that financing costs should be analyzed not only in aggregate but also by financing segment when assessing the structural consequences of revenue concentration.

title: Women in Office, Women in Markets: Female Leadership and Stock Market Participation

detail.abstract: We examine the impact of rising female political representation on women's stock market participation. Combining quasi-random variation from close mixed-gender elections in Indian state legislative assemblies with a stacked difference-in-differences approach, we find that a narrow female victory raises local women's stock market participation. The effect is stronger for single women and those residing in states with higher levels of gender discrimination. Mechanism analyses support a role model channel, whereby female electoral victories enhance women's financial aspirations and self-confidence. We find no evidence of short-run wealth losses.

title: Beat the Machine III: Robust Decisions Under Model Uncertainty Preregistered Temporal Replication of a MaxMin Decision Layer for Equity Selection
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Beat the Machine III: Robust Decisions Under Model Uncertainty Preregistered Temporal Replication of a MaxMin Decision Layer for Equity Selection

No external commercial sponsor, institutional funder, brokerage, asset manager, or other financial organization influenced the study design, analysis, interpretation, or reporting. No external funding was received for this study.
declarations.funderStatement: Anyone or Any

detail.abstract: Modern machine-learning systems increasingly produce calibrated scores, quantiles, and uncertainty estimates, yet the final action is often still obtained by ranking a point prediction and selecting the largest values. This paper studies a different question: whether realized decision quality can be improved without retraining the predictive model, solely by changing how a frozen probabilistic information state is converted into action. We introduce MM1, a preregistered MaxMin decision layer for Top-K equity selection. MM1 receives only frozen Phase-2 ex-ante signals: a baseline point estimate, a calibrated lower-tail estimate, baseline rank, and the promoted probabilistic guardrail. For each eligible candidate, the gap between the baseline and calibrated lower-tail estimate defines an asset-specific downside width. A budgeted adversarial uncertainty set then permits a limited fraction of selected positions to realize downside simultaneously. MM1 chooses the exact-K subset that maximizes its own worst-case mean value, while preserving a preregistered fallback and deterministic tie hierarchy. The predictive models, calibration offset, guardrail threshold, uncertainty budget, objective, optimizer semantics, and promotion criterion were frozen before realized outcomes were accessed. On the preregistered V5 temporal holdout, MM1 improved realized Top-K target-model value relative to the promoted Phase-2 guardrail by 0.05725 and increased hit rate by 5.49 percentage points. A preregistered news-event-cluster bootstrap produced a 95% interval for the value difference of [0.04347, 0.07486], although ticker-cluster sensitivity was materially wider and included zero. The identical frozen MM1 policy was then evaluated prospectively on the non-overlapping V6 holdout, with no V5-driven retuning. MM1 again improved realized decision value, by 0.11065, and increased hit rate by 15.86 percentage points. These results support temporal replication of positive incremental decision value from a robust decision layer relative to an already-promoted probabilistic ranking rule. The study does not establish absolute profitability, causal market effects, or uniform robustness across dependency structures. More broadly, the findings motivate a separation between prediction and decision: the machine may estimate uncertainty, but the decision rule still determines how that uncertainty is acted upon.

title: Heterogeneous Agent-based Modelling of Financial Fire Sales
affiliations: , Bank of England and Bank of England

detail.title: Heterogeneous Agent-based Modelling of Financial Fire Sales

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have no interests to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: The research required no funding.

detail.abstract: We develop a detailed agent-based model of financial fire sales that incorporates heterogeneous trading strategies, default mechanisms, and idiosyncratic shocks to asset prices and bank cash holdings. We introduce a novel metric to quantify the overall market environment, which influences individual bank health and target capital ratios. Using this framework, we analyse the impact of three key phenomena on bank default rates: (i) different trading strategies during crises; (ii) cash floors (not directly comparable to regulatory liquidity requirements); and (iii) post quantitative tightening (QT) environment with less reserves in the banking system. Our results provide insights into the interaction between market dynamics, regulatory constraints, and financial stability. We find that there are significant differences in default rates according to the trading strategy followed, with some performing significantly worse than others. Cash floor effects, in our setup, depend on their level. Partly driven by including inflationary cash devaluation dynamics in the model, increasing cash floors up to a certain level lowers the rate of defaults, after which increasing the level further can lead to adverse effects on default rates. Lastly, lower stock of reserves (post QT environment) in our setup makes banks less leveraged and lowers default rates in times of stress.

title: When Market Rates Rise: Deposit Repricing Across Banks and the Stablecoin Rewards Debate
affiliations: George Mason University - Buchanan Center Political Economy

detail.title: When Market Rates Rise: Deposit Repricing Across Banks and the Stablecoin Rewards Debate

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship with any people or organizations that may have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, this study.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: Would rewards on payment stablecoins, digital assets designed to maintain a fixed value against the dollar, place some banks' funding at greater risk than others? The policy debate focuses particularly on community banks. I examine one premise behind that concern: how banks changed the interest paid on deposits when market rates rose. Using regulatory filings for 3,771 FDIC-insured commercial banks and savings institutions, I construct each institution's implied average deposit rate, defined as annualized interest expense on domestic deposits per dollar of domestic deposits. Deposit-rate pass-through is the percentage of the 4.94-percentage-point increase in the three-month Treasury bill rate from the fourth quarter of 2021 through the third quarter of 2024 that was reflected in this rate. Giving each bank equal weight, median pass-through was 35.2 percent among 3,513 FDIC-designated community banks and 53.8 percent among 74 institutions with $10 billion to $250 billion in assets. Twelve of the 74 institutions also carry the FDIC community-bank designation. The 18.6-percentage-point shortfall for community banks is statistically distinguishable from zero. Its 95 percent confidence interval, which summarizes statistical uncertainty, ranges from 13.0 to 22.6 percentage points. Community-bank pass-through was also lower at the twenty-fifth and seventy-fifth percentiles of the two bank distributions. Lower pass-through could reflect relatively stable, relationship-based deposits or banks with less need, willingness, or ability to match a competing return. Community banks also had higher median net deposit growth, which weighs against the simplest interpretation that lower pass-through reflected an inability to retain deposits but does not distinguish among these explanations. These historical comparisons do not estimate the effect of stablecoin rewards on deposit flows or bank lending.

title: The Quiet Ledger: How the World Is De-Dollarizing Through Plumbing Rather Than Proclamation, 2000 to 2026

detail.title: The Quiet Ledger: How the World Is De-Dollarizing Through Plumbing Rather Than Proclamation, 2000 to 2026

detail.abstract: The debate over de-dollarization has been conducted almost entirely in the wrong register. It asks whether the dollar is about to lose its status as the world's reserve currency, finds that it is not, and concludes that de-dollarization is a myth. The headline indicators support that conclusion. The dollar held 57.13 percent of allocated official reserves in the first quarter of 2026, a share that rose from the previous quarter. It stood on one side of 89.2 percent of foreign exchange transactions in April 2025, more than in 2022. It settled just over half of international payments on SWIFT in August 2026, close to four fifths of trade finance, and nearly sixty percent of payments on SWIFT's alternative measure. This paper argues that these are the wrong instruments for detecting the change now under way. Contemporary de-dollarization is not a currency substitution event but an infrastructure event. It proceeds not through declarations of monetary independence, which have consistently failed, but through the construction of sovereign payment and settlement rails that move value between jurisdictions without passing through United States correspondent banking, United States clearing, or United States law. What is being built is not a replacement for the dollar as a unit of account or a store of value. It is a replacement for the dollar as a compulsory route. Dollar dominance was never one thing. It is five separable functions, and the statistics that dominate this debate measure four of them. The fifth, the settlement route, is the one that has changed, and no institution publishes a series for it. Tracing the period from unchallenged dollar supremacy in 2000 through the disconnection of Iranian banks from the financial messaging system in 2012, the immobilization of Russian central bank reserves in 2022, and the mandatory rollout of the digital ruble on September 1, 2026, the paper finds a consistent pattern: states that announce alternatives fail, and states that build them while denying any such intention succeed at the margin. It examines the two military conflicts of 2026, in Venezuela and Iran, as the most direct available test of the proposition that the dollar rests on force, finding the popular version of that thesis unproven and a narrower version difficult to dismiss. And it concludes that the terminal architecture is not a BRICS common currency, which no member seriously wants, but interoperability: the linking of sovereign digital currencies and domestic payment systems into a mesh that can clear bilateral trade outside any Western regime. India's proposal to put that linkage before the September 2026 New Delhi summit is the clearest expression of the design to date. Whether it succeeds is uncertain. That it is being attempted is not.

detail.abstract: Property taxation has returned to the centre of public debate as housing values have risen sharply since the 2008 crisis. Existing research has identified land appreciation as a central driver of wealth accumulation, yet across Southern Europe, the taxation of economic land rents remains largely underexplored. In Spain, the Impuesto sobre Bienes Inmuebles (IBI) is levied on registered cadastral values that are revised infrequently and at uneven intervals, so the effective base departs from market value in ways that are neither uniform nor neutral across households. Drawing on Henry George's concept of land rent, this paper examines how increases in land value are captured by particular households across urban Spain. Using newly available household-level registry data and a simplified asset pricing model, the paper provides a distributional analysis of land and property underassessment. The analysis first tests for vertical inequity in the cadastral base across urban Spain and then builds a microsimulation to estimate the capitalised value of the resulting tax saving and to trace its distribution across housing wealth, income, age and location, alongside a stylised income-tax-linked scheme for recycling the additional revenue. The final simulations suggest that reorienting taxation towards property and away from labour has the potential to improve progressivity and reduce disparities in housing wealth.

title: A Sin Ban, Not a Sin Tax? Consumption and Incidence of SNAP Soda Restrictions

detail.abstract: We study the first statewide SNAP restrictions on sweetened beverages and candy. Restricted spending falls 11 percent; calories and sugar fall 5-8 percent. Substitution is asymmetric: eligible fruit drinks partly offset soda declines, while candy restrictions reduce purchases of eligible snacks. Retailers barely change shelf prices. Losing SNAP's sales-tax exemption raises tax-inclusive prices only 1.9 percent. Spending declines are larger at retailers with greater SNAP use and remain large online, where checkout stigma is less salient. Nationwide adoption would impose 13 percent of the out-ofpocket burden of an equivalent excise tax, while welfare gains reach roughly $1.1 billion annually.

title: Where Does the Cost of Equity Actually Move? Beta, the Risk-Free Rate, and Twenty Years of Indian Automobiles

detail.title: Where Does the Cost of Equity Actually Move? Beta, the Risk-Free Rate, and Twenty Years of Indian Automobiles

detail.abstract: Every valuation of an Indian automobile company involves calculating the cost of equity, which depends on beta. Beta is usually taken from a data source, estimated using whatever time period the source uses by default, and then used in the valuation. However, no one has documented how well this approach has worked over a full market cycle in India. There is also no clear evidence on whether the usual estimation period continues to work when the underlying risk of the automobile sector changes. This paper examines both questions using data from 71 automobile companies, a 425-company control group, and a complete monthly series of the Indian 10-year government bond yield from February 2005 to June 2026. The sector's cost of equity ranged from 11.32% in 2009 to 15.80% in 2018-a difference of 448 basis points. If cash flows are assumed to grow at 5% forever, this difference in the cost of equity changes the valuation multiple from 15.8× to 9.3×. In other words, the same cash flows can be worth 71% more at one end of the period than the other. Interestingly, the lowest cost of equity occurred in the year after the global financial crisis, rather than during a calm market period. Indian automobiles stopped behaving like a defensive sector around 2016. From 2007 to 2015, the sector's median beta was below the market beta in every year, by an average of 0.150. From 2016 onwards, the sector's beta has been at or above the market beta. A formal structural break test identifies 2016 as the break point. About half of the change in beta was due to changes in the overall market. The difference-indifferences result against the control group is +0.192. This remains almost the same at +0.1916 when the analysis is limited to a fixed group of companies that were present throughout all twenty years. This means that changes in the composition of the automobile sector do not explain the increase. The conventional estimation window does not work well, but only during the period when the sector’s risk is changing. At the 2016, 2017, and 2018 estimation points, using a ten-year window results in an error of about 0.17 in beta compared with using a two-year window. At every other estimation point from 2013 to 2024, the difference is very small- less than 0.01. The size of this effect depends on how much each company’s own risk changed. When the change in each company’s beta is compared with the additional error caused by using the longer window, the relationship has a slope of 0.539 (t = 5.01, p = 0.00001, R² = 0.34). The relationship is consistent across beta-change quartiles. Companies whose risk did not change did not face any additional error from using the longer window. The practical conclusion is narrow and useful. The length of the estimation window does not matter much when a sector’s systematic risk is stable, which is true most of the time. However, it matters a lot for roughly three years after the sector’s risk changes. This is also the period when an analyst is least likely to notice that the sector’s underlying risk has changed.

title: Filtering Without Recursion and Some of Its Uses in Financial Economics

detail.abstract: We develop a filter for time series, defined at each time t as the minimizer of a discounted convex combination of observed and expected losses. The filter can be estimated by simulation to an arbitrary level of accuracy in O(1) flops at each time point t & can be run for all values t = 1, ..., T in parallel. These methods are applied to robustly compute a preaveraged price process from the more than 1.5 million trades made on a single financial asset in a single day where the noise's variance is infinite. It yields a flat "volatility signature" plot, down to the 1 second level, so the microstructure noise no longer biases the volatility estimate. This is not true when linear methods are employed.

title: Decision Technology as a Service (DTaaS): When the Decision Becomes the Product A Conceptual Review of Decision-Centric Enterprise Architecture in the Agentic Era

detail.title: Decision Technology as a Service (DTaaS): When the Decision Becomes the Product A Conceptual Review of Decision-Centric Enterprise Architecture in the Agentic Era

detail.abstract: Enterprise technology has automated almost everything around a decision while leaving the decision itself oddly fragmented. Data platforms record reality, analytics describe it, machine learning predicts it, generative AI explains it, and agentic systems increasingly act upon it. Yet organizations can possess excellent data, sophisticated models, and hundreds of agents and still make mediocre decisions. This conceptual review argues that the next useful unit of enterprise architecture is not the model, application, workflow, or agent, but the decision. The paper develops Decision Technology as a Service (DTaaS) as an organizational and technological architecture for producing governed, executable, observable, and learnable decisions. DTaaS is deliberately distinguished from classical Decision Support Systems, Decision Intelligence, AI-as-a-Service, Decision-as-a-Service implementations that expose rules through APIs, and current agentic-AI frameworks. It treats AI agents as participants in a broader decision-production system rather than as the product itself. The review synthesizes recent work from SSRN and arXiv on agentic finance, delegated autonomy, decision governance, auditability, human-AI delegation, and decision intelligence, together with Russian-language research on AI-enabled decision-support systems. It introduces a set of conceptual constructs: the Decision Supply Chain, decision latency, judgment debt, decision provenance, the Decision Factory, and a decision-sovereignty boundary. Banking is used as the main illustrative domain because credit, pricing, risk, compliance, capital, liquidity, and delegated authority expose the difference between prediction and decision particularly clearly. The central claim is intentionally simple: AI is becoming abundant; accountable judgment is not. The competitive advantage of the agentic enterprise may therefore depend less on how much AI it owns than on how coherently it turns intelligence into consequential action.

title: From Technological Abundance to Institutional Inclusion:The Social Distribution Mechanism of the Technological Dividend

detail.title: From Technological Abundance to Institutional Inclusion:The Social Distribution Mechanism of the Technological Dividend

detail.abstract: Embodied intelligence integrates algorithmic capability with physical agents and can reshape the means of labor, labor processes, and the supply of goods and services. This prospect has encouraged a technological-abundance narrative in which large-scale deployment of intelligent machines is assumed to translate directly into broadly shared prosperity. This article challenges that inference. Productive capacity determines what can be produced; ownership, distributional institutions, and public services shape who controls the resulting resources and how households gain access to them. Grounded in historical materialism and the author's Life-Spirit Structure Theory, the article develops the concept of “wealth-value divergence” through three propositions. The Use-Value Proliferation Proposition holds that embodied intelligence can sharply expand use-value output per unit of living labor. The Value-Form Constraint Proposition, formulated within a Marxian theory of value, holds that automation does not by itself resolve the social and institutional conditions through which commodity value, income, and purchasing power are formed and distributed. The Distributional Rupture Proposition holds that when productive expansion outpaces institutions that distribute income and access, a structural gap can emerge between material abundance and effective social inclusion. The article then identifies four mechanisms that mediate the conversion of technological dividends into common prosperity: control over intelligent means of production, distribution of technological returns, decoupling of basic public services from employment status, and adaptive governance. Comparative institutional analysis suggests that institutional systems differ in their capacity to adjust across these mechanisms. In dialogue with Mazzucato, Piketty, Stiglitz, Rawls, and Sen, the article argues that technological abundance becomes inclusive only through institutional conversion rather than technological capability alone. Within China's policy framework, common prosperity supplies an explicit distributive objective, but implementation remains contingent on addressing platform and compute concentration, employment transitions, regional digital divides, and public participation. The article concludes with proposals for universal access to public computing infrastructure, ex ante sharing of technological returns, portable social protection, and employment-impact assessment.

detail.abstract: Retail central bank digital currency (CBDC) can displace commercial-bank deposits, but the central bank can return the displaced funding to banks through refinancing. Does one-for-one replacement also preserve bank lending? I study this question in a nonlinear New Keynesian model with bank credit and an occasionally binding prudential-liquidity constraint. One-for-one refinancing eliminates the CBDC-induced funding displacement exactly, but funding neutrality need not imply credit neutrality. Combining the bank balance sheet, the refinancing rule, and the prudential-liquidity condition yields an exact matched-path decomposition of the bank-credit gap. The decomposition shows that deposits and central-bank refinancing need not provide the same effective liquidity capacity because deposit stocks, settlement outflows, lending, and the liquidity transformation generated by refinancing affect prudential headroom differently. The refinancing rate that most closely reproduces the counterfactual lending path is therefore state dependent and can lie above, at, or below one. Quantitatively, one-for-one refinancing can be nearly credit neutral under short-lived prudential stress yet generate a lending overshoot when stress persists. Funding neutrality, credit preservation, credit neutrality, and welfare are consequently distinct policy objectives.

detail.abstract: Green hydrogen mandates are widely enacted but rarely costed at a specific facility. We measure the cost of the renewable-only requirement at the Intermountain Power Project, a repowered 840 MW plant contracted to fire a hydrogen blend produced solely from renewable energy and stored in salt caverns. Using 17,544 hours of aligned wholesale prices, site-calibrated solar and wind generation, and hourly grid carbon intensity, we compare configurations delivering identical annual hydrogen. Grid-sourced hydrogen costs $3.87/kg; dedicated renewable hydrogen costs $8.67/kg, a premium of $4.79/kg or 124 percent. The premium arises from costlier dedicated energy and an electrolyzer whose utilization falls from 97 to 50 percent, not from storage, which is the least influential cost. Partial mandates are convex, since a shared electrolyzer serves both supplies. The mandate abates carbon at roughly $562 per tonne, nineteen times prevailing allowance prices, locating its justification outside carbon policy.

title: A Machine-Verified Claims Ledger for Trading-Strategy Research

detail.title: A Machine-Verified Claims Ledger for Trading-Strategy Research

detail.abstract: Trading-strategy research has a reproducibility problem that is structural, not incidental: the researcher controls the number of trials, the cost assumptions, and the reporting, and every incentive points toward publishing the survivor. The methodology literature has quantified the damage - the probability of backtest overfitting, the multiple-testing haircuts - but tooling that enforces discipline inside a working research programme has lagged. We describe a governance layer we built and have operated across an 18-month futures-trading research programme: a machine-verified claims ledger in which every published number is a claim object binding (i) the number to a value re-derived live from the evidence files that produced it, (ii) three independent verifications required to fail for different reasons, including a falsification test, and (iii) a mandatory declared blind spot. The ledger re-derives all 79 current claims offline in minutes, with no market data; continuous integration blocks any change that breaks one; a claim whose evidence file is not version-controlled is rejected structurally; and a self-test replays five real historical defects and requires the harness to reject each one for the right reason - a gate that has never failed being, in our experience, the most dangerous object in a research pipeline. Around the ledger we operate pre-registration with dated, append-only amendments; mandatory power analysis before any negative verdict; dumb controls and noise checks before any positive; stressed-cost headlines; and a live track record that is out-of-sample by construction, with parameters hash-frozen under a signed protocol before the evaluation data exists. We illustrate the system with cases where it changed the conclusion - including a pre-registered 225-cell null on opening-range breakout and a forward study in which our own deployed champions decayed to 17.6% of their in-sample rate - and argue the pattern generalizes to any field whose results are selected before they are reported.

detail.abstract: Common use of artificial-intelligence (AI) systems creates forecast errors that need not diversify across decision makers. Aggregate common error is q ′ Bq, where B is the model-error covariance matrix and q records reliance-weighted economic exposure. Vendor concentration is sufficient only under restrictive symmetry, and even fixed userlevel model probabilities and vendor shares leave a joint assignment margin. Qualityequivalent routing can therefore reduce aggregate error without lowering individual forecast quality. We show that this ordering survives endogenous trading intensity in an aggregate-signal market. In a heterogeneous rational-expectations equilibrium, however, price and demand loadings respond to routing; we derive the equilibrium-adjusted routing gradient, characterize when covariance and price rankings agree, and show why they can differ. Rational price learning attenuates but cannot eliminate shared model errors, while greater precision improves price discovery at fixed assignment. Fragility consequently requires an extensive-margin response. A two-model selection equilibrium identifies an open region in which migration toward the more common-error-intensive family overturns the direct information gain. A six-checkpoint historical macroeconomic panel illustrates estimation of B and its allocation content, while its registered routing and packet-quality limitations make the evidence exploratory rather than confirmatory.

detail.abstract: Online discourse is increasingly shaped by artificial agents that participate alongside humans in contesting and enforcing social norms. Whether AI agents can function as normative signals — making norms salient and motivating human enforcement — is unknown. In a pre-registered online experiment (N = 1,176), UK-based participants joined a forum thread in which a false headline was either left unchallenged, corrected by a human user, or corrected by an AI agent. We provide evidence that AI corrections are equivalent to human corrections in updating observers’ normative beliefs about the appropriateness of correcting misinformation and in improving recognition of false content. Both sources also substantially increase observers’ own corrective behavior relative to no correction. However, the equivalence breaks down when we look at norm enforcement: humans show a roughly 6-percentage-point advantage in mobilizing corrections. A follow-up survey (N = 301) suggests this gap tracks perceived legitimacy — human correctors are rated warmer, more credible, and more authentic. Together, the findings show that AI corrections can transmit the informational and normative content of a social correction as effectively as humans can, while raising the possibility that they are less effective at mobilizing enforcement — a pattern consistent with differences in the perceived legitimacy of the correcting agent.

detail.abstract: We analyze an infinite-horizon model of legislative bargaining in which the size of the pie depends on the coalition that supports it. In the baseline model there are two types of legislators: active and passive. The inclusion of an active legislator increases the size of the pie, whereas passive legislators do not affect it. Thus, the pie consists of a fixed part, as in canonical legislative bargaining models, and a variable part that depends on the number of active legislators included in the coalition, as in coalitional bargaining models. In equilibrium, active legislators demand a greater compensation, so proposers trade off maximizing the size of the pie against maximizing their share of it. Equilibria can exhibit two kinds of inefficiency: size inefficiency (coalitions are too small) and composition inefficiency (coalitions include too few active legislators given their size). Composition inefficiency, which existing models rule out or overlook, is sustained by the fear of exclusion from future coalitions: proposers randomize between passive and active partners, which disciplines the compensation active legislators can demand. Both inefficiencies arise when the fixed part of the pie is sufficiently large relative to its variable part or legislators are sufficiently patient.

title: How Far Can a Judgment Travel? Sovereign Immunity and the Architecture of Transnational Legal Effect

detail.title: How Far Can a Judgment Travel? Sovereign Immunity and the Architecture of Transnational Legal Effect

detail.abstract: A judgment may be valid, final, and legally binding and yet remain incapable of producing every consequence ordinarily associated with adjudicatory authority. Sovereign immunity reveals this phenomenon with unusual clarity. International and domestic legal systems distinguish jurisdiction from enforcement, consent to adjudication from consent to measures of constraint, recognition from execution, and, in some contexts, post-judgment discovery from attachment. These distinctions are doctrinally familiar. Their combined structural significance, however, has received less systematic attention. This Article argues that transnational adjudication can be better understood by shifting the unit of analysis from the judgment as an indivisible legal object to the distinct effects that legal authority seeks to produce across sovereign legal orders. Those effects need not travel together. They may be coupled at one institutional stage and decoupled at another according to jurisdictional, sovereign, functional, procedural, and patrimonial considerations. Sovereign immunity is therefore examined not merely as an exception to judicial effectiveness, but as a particularly revealing instance of a broader architecture of differentiated transnational legal effect. Drawing on the Brazilian private international law tradition represented by Haroldo Valladão and Wilson de Souza Campos Batalha, and placing it in dialogue with Harold Hongju Koh's account of transnational legal process and Jack Goldsmith's emphasis on domestic institutions and sovereign authority, the Article develops the idea of controlled legal continuity across otherwise discontinuous legal orders. The argument is tested against the International Court of Justice's judgment in Jurisdictional Immunities of the State, Brazilian Supreme Court and Superior Court of Justice decisions, United States sovereign-immunity jurisprudence, and the distinct treaty regime governing international organizations. The claim is deliberately limited. This Article does not propose a new classification of judgments or a new general theory of sovereign immunity. It offers an analytical lens for understanding how different consequences associated with the same legal authority may encounter different limits when projected across sovereign legal orders. The relevant question is therefore not simply whether a judgment travels, but which effect travels, through which institution, against which person or asset, and how far the law permits that effect to go.

detail.abstract: Collective decisions in diverse and conflict-prone settings often compress disagreement into preference counts or a single aggregate, even though the intensity and location of resistance may matter for subsequent cooperation. This conceptual-methodological paper derives the Sustainable Decision Finder (SDF) from ECOOPx, a six-dimensional framework for analysing cooperation through Trust, Shared Vision, Resonance, Communication, Organisation and Urgency. SDF is specified as a layered architecture that combines graded resistance assessment, retention of the resistance distribution, an extreme-resistance inspection layer, a proposal-level escalation rule, optional ECOOPx-based driver diagnosis, recursive proposal revision and longitudinal evaluation of implementation. Analytical counterexamples compare linear-sum, median, convex and minimax aggregation. A fully reproducible synthetic simulation of 100 students in an international classroom shows that plurality preference and resistance aggregation can select different candidates and that aggregator choice encodes distinct normative priorities. Across 500 synthetic seeds, minimax frequently favours the passive option when it has few strong opponents, illustrating a tension between worst-case protection and change. The paper does not claim empirical validation. Instead, seven falsifiable propositions specify what evidence would make individual SDF layers unnecessary. The contribution is therefore a testable group-decision architecture in which resistance is treated not only as a quantity to minimise but as information to inspect, diagnose and, when warranted, return to deliberation.

detail.abstract: The premium the world pays for U.S. Treasuries has decoupled from the premium it pays for the dollar. Measured against foreign sovereigns on a covered-interest-parity basis, the Treasury premium has been negative since 2021; the dollar premium has not. The funding instruments of American power are therefore under measurable pressure, and the mechanism is fiscal quantity rather than fiscal credibility: the stock of Treasuries has grown faster than the intermediation capacity and the relative supply of alternatives that once absorbed it at a premium. A companion paper argued that China's decline is largely endogenous and that the United States can accelerate or retard it only at the margin, so that American success depends less on what Washington does to Beijing than on whether it preserves its own structural advantages. This paper tests that claim in the domain where it is cleanest. Fiscal deterioration is the purest case of strategic self-harm: it depletes the advantages on which American statecraft depends, with no foreign cause. The paper's contribution is a strategic-solvency threshold — defined by the joint behavior of five observable series, with stated trigger values, rather than by any debt-to-GDP level — together with the specification of the object that threshold prices, which has split in two. The April 2025 episode, in which Treasuries and the dollar sold off together in price terms while the two convenience premiums moved apart, is examined as the one observation that bears directly on whether the split will hold. The threshold is approached on the Treasury side and not crossed on the dollar side. The deciding constraint on American power has become internal, and the fiscal path is where that is most visible, because the remedy is known, has been executed before, and was abandoned.

detail.abstract:
In 2025-26 the United Kingdom spent £96.9 billion on central government net debt interest on the Office for National Statistics measure, and £109.7 billion on the Office for Budget Responsibility measure. The OBR forecasts £137.1 billion by 2030-31. Debt interest is the second largest item of public spending and the only one that funds no public service.

Three things drive the bill. Index-linked gilts stood at £672.7 billion in uplifted nominal value at 31 March 2026, 23.9 per cent of the portfolio, the highest share in the G7 and about twice the next highest. Central bank reserves, which averaged £664.9 billion in 2025-26, earn Bank Rate, so Bank Rate is now the effective interest rate on roughly a quarter of the national debt. And the Asset Purchase Facility, which returned about £124 billion to the Exchequer while Bank Rate sat below the coupons it held, is now indemnified at an estimated lifetime net cost of £164 billion by the end of 2036.

This paper sets out ten measures, models them as a unified plan against the OBR's March 2026 baseline to 2050-51 under five scenarios, states who bears what cost, and drafts the legislation that would be required. Every formula is written out in an appendix and the model is published in full, so the results can be checked rather than taken on trust.

Use of AI tools. The analysis, the model, the figures and the argument in this paper are the author's own. A large language model was used to edit and format Part 11, the draft Bill, so that its structure, numbering and drafting conventions follow those of United Kingdom legislation. No AI tool produced any insight, analysis, interpretation or conclusion, and no AI tool is an author. The author is responsible for the whole of the text.

title: Central Banking in the Islamic World: From Late Adoption to Contemporary Practice

detail.title: Central Banking in the Islamic World: From Late Adoption to Contemporary Practice
detail.abstract: This article examines the evolution of central banking in the Islamic world, tracing its late emergence compared to Europe and its contemporary adaptations to Islamic finance. While early European central banks arose in response to fiscal and military needs, Muslim-majority societies faced delayed adoption due to colonial domination, limited capital formation, and reliance on traditional monetary practices. The Ottoman Empire’s gradual transition—from coinage-based stability to paper money, external debt, and ultimately the Imperial Ottoman Bank—illustrates how fiscal distress and foreign influence shaped the trajectory of central banking. Institutional factors such as partnership-based business structures, Islamic inheritance law, and the role of waqf further constrained capital accumulation, though colonialism and the Industrial Revolution proved equally decisive. Today, most Muslim-majority countries operate conventional central banks, but with Shariah-compliant alternatives to support dual banking systems. Malaysia and Pakistan, for instance, have developed innovative liquidity tools such as commodity murabaha, mudarabah-based operations, and sukuk issuance to integrate Islamic finance into national monetary policy. Proposals for fully equity-based, interest-free central banking highlight both the ethical promise and operational challenges of aligning monetary policy with Islamic principles. The article concludes that while hybrid models prevail, Islamic finance continues to influence debates on stability, risk-sharing, and financial reform.

detail.abstract: An adviser who warns that a task is difficult may become harder to evaluate when her advice is followed more thoroughly. We study a long-lived adviser and successive short-lived workers who choose between standard and intensive implementation. Standard implementation reveals whether the warning was correct and gives the next worker an opportunity to acquire cost-saving practical knowledge. Intensive implementation protects the project but produces only occasional evidence about the adviser. We construct a stationary sequential equilibrium in which the adviser initially accepts an informative implementation, withholds the next project after her reputation improves, and resumes recommendations once inherited know-how has been lost. The interruption is chosen because it changes the successor's implementation decision: preserving know-how reverses the adviser's preference at the relevant history. All realized evidence remains public. Weak subsequent evidence eventually ends the low-ability adviser's protection, but this can take a long time.

detail.abstract: The ASEAN Community Vision 2045: Our Shared Future signals a strategic pivot toward a 20year horizon, set against a poly-crisis context of geopolitical rivalry, climate change, and technological disruption. This article assesses the Vision's five commitments: Political-Security, Economic, Socio-Cultural, Connectivity, and Institutional Strengthening through the Critical Institutional Analysis and Development (CIAD) framework, with attention to two architectural innovations. The first is a modular six-document compendium that enables flexible five-year implementation cycles. The second is the operationalization of Summit decision-making procedures for serious Charter breaches, emergency situations, and cases in which consensus cannot be reached, all without formally amending the ASEAN Charter. Economically, the bloc retains its long-term ambition of becoming the world's fourth-largest economy by 2045, supported by DEFA, the Blue Economy agenda, and green-transition commitments. The documents and supporting literature, however, point to substantial hurdles, including the persistent Myanmar crisis, a major infrastructure financing gap, digital and development divides, and demographic bifurcation. Realizing this resilient and people-centered community will depend on the political will to empower the ASEAN Secretariat, mobilize sustainable financing, and reconcile strategic aspiration with institutional implementation capacity.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces strategic unreasonableness as a deliberate trading tool for situations where rational behavior has become predictable and therefore exploitable by AI trading systems. Drawing on game theory, military history, negotiation tactics, and business strategy, we establish strategic unreasonableness as a recognized phenomenon across domains. We then formalize the concept for trading and test it empirically using Monte Carlo simulation on SPY data (2015-2025) with a Donchian channel strategy. The results show that introducing 10-15% random deviation from rational behavior increases unpredictability to 0.97 (near maximum entropy) while reducing the Sharpe ratio by only 0.03. This holds even after accounting for 0.1% transaction costs per trade. The paper concludes that against pattern-learning AI adversaries, controlled randomness is not the absence of strategy-it is the optimal strategy for preserving edge while avoiding exploitation.

detail.abstract: The 2026 National Drug Control Strategy identifies fragmented, siloed data systems and limited analytical capacity as structural weaknesses in the U.S. government's ability to screen and monitor pharmaceutical and precursor-chemical imports, and calls for modernized, standardized data systems and expanded risk-based screening. For a structurally similar problem, financial institutions have spent twenty years developing a nearly identical capability: identifying anomalous cross-border transactions, reconciling multi-jurisdiction compliance documentation, monitoring exception rates against specified KPIs and SLAs, and scoring a transaction using its own financial attributes, corridor, counterparty, payment memo, structuring pattern, under Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money-laundering (AML) regimes. This paper argues that the toolkit is directly transferable to pharmaceutical and precursor-chemical import screening using a structured cross-domain mapping methodology, treating financial-crimes transaction monitoring as the source domain and pharmaceutical/precursor-chemical import screening as the target domain. It proposes a framework based on five components, three of which are expressed as named, itemized scores: a Trade Risk Score built from the shipment's own declared attributes against the importer's baseline, a Documentation Risk Score built from cross-system completeness and consistency, a Financial Risk Score built from the payment's own financial attributes origin, beneficiary, corridor, third-party payer, timing, counterparty history, joined to the shipment via a shared invoice or purchase-order reference where available, or through entity resolution otherwise, an entity-resolution layer linking importer, exporter, financial-counterparty, and beneficial-owner identities across filings and payments, and KPI/SLA-based exception dashboards. The three scores combine into a single Integrated Import Risk Score, mirroring the composite fraud-and-AML scorecards banks already run. The study examines FinCEN's own Bank Secrecy Act data mining on fentanyl-related illicit finance, which in 2024 identified about $1.4 billion in suspected transactions with distinguishable wire-corridor, payment-memo, and shell-company typologies. This is not done as a distant analogy, but rather as proof of the financial-transaction signals that the Financial Risk Score would try to include, joined when feasible to shipment-side declarations. It shows how the shipment-side components could be layered onto existing infrastructure, CBP's Automated Commercial Environment, FDA's PREDICT risk-targeting system, and the INCB's PEN Online precursor pre-export notification system, in a way that could potentially leverage existing statutory and reporting infrastructure, subject to agency-specific legal and governance review, while the financial-data-integration component would require a legally authorized interagency data-sharing mechanism between Treasury/FinCEN and the trade agencies; this paper does not determine whether additional statutory or regulatory authority would be required. The paper situates its contribution against the closest existing research, including the NSF-funded FIND-M project and a broader academic literature on trade-based money laundering, financial-crime analytics, explainable AI, illicit-supply-chain networks, counterfeit medicines, and data-driven customs risk management, and identifies the specific gap in that literature its framework addresses. It concludes with the framework's implications for regulators and industry compliance teams and identifies what would be needed to test it against real institutional data.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of monetary policy announcements (MPAs) on household inflation expectations using microdata from the Swiss Consumer Sentiment Survey. Employing an event study approach, we reveal an asymmetric response: while policy rate hikes or decisions to keep rates constant reduce household inflation expectations, rate cuts fail to elicit a reaction. The effect is particularly robust for short-term expectations, with a much less clear-cut influence on long-term expectations. Households across the expectation distribution - both moderate and extreme - react to announcements, indicating a broad impact. We find that household reactions are driven primarily by the anticipated component of policy rate changes, whereas surprising moves tend to be interpreted as signals of new information regarding inflationary pressure. Finally, we report that demographic heterogeneity matters: the effect of MPAs is driven by German-speaking households and tertiary-educated individuals, while others show no consistent response, underscoring the importance of targeted communication strategies for effective monetary policy transmission.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the composition of taxation when the government cannot fully commit to respecting private returns after investment. A fiscal authority must finance a given expenditure from labor and capital income. Ordinary tax receipts are protected, but an opportunistic executive can seize part of the remaining capital payment. We show that a revenue-neutral increase in the capital tax raises the probability of compliance whenever the labor tax is below its local, fixed-wage revenue peak, provided the equilibrium remains on a regular mixing branch. This result does not depend on the elasticity of substitution between capital and labor. The same reform can raise investment: the gain in expected retention must outweigh the decline in the opportunist's continuation gain as compliance becomes less informative. We also characterize the Ramsey allocation conditional on full compliance. Limited commitment then imposes a ceiling on sustainable capital payments, rather than a general lower bound on the statutory capital-tax rate. Finally, we distinguish a change in the authority's concern for the future from an increase in both actors' patience. The former favors more informative policies when continuation welfare is convex; the latter has no unconditional direction in the reduced-form policy problem.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a sloshing-aware tube model predictive control (MPC) for spacecraft proximity operations, which sizes its constraint tightening from the propellant's slosh reaction and applies it only to the constraints that bind, the approach corridor and the pointing budget. A chaser closing on a Mars Sample Return interface carries propellant that sloshes relative to its hub, and a tube MPC certified against rigid-body disturbances cannot tell whether that motion matters. Earlier work flew the reference guidance in the General Mission Analysis Tool. To model the sloshing, the same ellipticalorbit rendezvous is flown here in Basilisk, a six-degree-of-freedom multibody simulator that represents the propellant with coupled slosh particles. Once a burn-delivery defect in the simulation loop is corrected, the rigid Basilisk plant reproduces the earlier campaign. Flown unchanged from homing to contact on the sloshing plant, the reference guidance misses the port by more on every seed, at almost no extra propellant. A frozen-liquid control suggests that most of this loss comes from the uncontrolled hub tumbling about the propellant's offset centre of mass rather than from the liquid itself, and a tube ablation on the same guidance is inconclusive at this sample size. A comparison of several controllers on the terminal and closing legs then isolates the slosh disturbance. Sizing the attitude tube's tightening from the slosh torque improves pointing accuracy in the final proximity approach by 12.8% over both nominal MPC and tube MPC, while the same tightening in translation changes nothing measurable. A horizon-selecting variant saves propellant, but pays for it with a slower arrival and more corridor excursions during the blind coast.

detail.abstract: Governments play a central role in modern market economies, making uncertainty surrounding fiscal, monetary, regulatory, and trade policies an important source of macroeconomic and financial instability. These dynamics are especially relevant in the context of the United States and China, whose economic scale and strategic rivalry increasingly shape global economic conditions. This paper examines the relationship between U.S. and Chinese economic policy uncertainty (EPU) within a cointegrated VAR framework. The results show that U.S. EPU, Chinese EPU, and global oil prices share a stable long-run relationship, but the adjustment process is asymmetric. Deviations from equilibrium are corrected primarily through changes in Chinese policy uncertainty, while U.S. EPU behaves as relatively weakly exogenous. Adjustment is gradual, with roughly one-third of disequilibrium corrected each quarter. The findings have implications for global governance, macroeconomic resilience, and international financial stability.
