affiliations: Kristiania University College

detail.title: Tax Base Erosion and Fiscal Capacity: Evidence from Early Modern Poland

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses historical archival tax registers (Atlas Fontium) and involves no human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how elite tax exemptions erode fiscal capacity. Newly digitized registers record rates and the taxable land separately for 18,000 villages in the sixteenthcentury Crown of Poland. I exploit the Livonian War's 50% rate increase, which noble estates could escape by reclassifying peasant land as tax-exempt demesne but royal estates could not. The tax base elasticity, approximately-0.4, is the first identified for an early modern economy; erosion absorbed one-third of wartime revenue gains and did not reverse. Displaced peasants reappeared in the registers as landless labor, a new fiscal channel behind the intensification of serfdom.

title: National Belonging Among Nepalis in Japan

detail.title: National Belonging Among Nepalis in Japan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest exists.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was partly funded by Japan Society for the Promotion of Science

detail.abstract: The article investigates national belonging among Nepalis in Japan, focusing on Nepali parents in the Greater Tokyo Area. Drawing on a conceptual framework rooted in nationalism studies and a selection of semi-structured interviews conducted with 63 Nepalis between March 2023 and April 2024, it reveals three aspects constitutive of their national belonging: 1) their perceived differences with the host population in terms of Japanese individualism and Nepali collectivism, 2) their adaptation to Japan accompanied by the valorization of their Nepali identity in view of the practicalities of life and the inaccessibility of Japaneseness, and 3) their negotiation of Nepaliness using a racial discourse and imagination with regard to their childrearing experiences in Japan. The study has a clear broader implication. It demonstrates that parenthood, as a major stage of the normative life course, has a significant and distinct bearing on national belonging among migrants. It suggests that national belonging among migrants is more productively studied by considering not only the social experiences of migrants in their host country and its dominant discourse of nationalism, but also their life course. It thus calls for increased life course sensitivity in nationalism studies.

title: The Factor Hierarchy System: A Unified Theoretical Framework for Cross-Disciplinary Complex Systems Research

detail.title: The Factor Hierarchy System: A Unified Theoretical Framework for Cross-Disciplinary Complex Systems Research

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract:
This paper systematically expounds the “Factor Hierarchy System” as a unified conceptual framework for cross-disciplinary complex systems research. The system is built upon forty-seven preceding papers and consists of four components: the Information Isomorphism Law (epistemological foundation), which reveals that statistical structure carries information about regime structure; the Factor Hierarchy Law (ontology), which clarifies that factor functions divide into regime factors and execution factors; the Testability Principle (epistemological standard), which stipulates that claims about factor importance must undergo regime-dependence testing; and the Testability Norms (methodology), which provides standardized testing procedures across six functional dimensions. The four exhibit a four-layer progression of “epistemological foundation → ontology → epistemological standard → methodology,” with a minimal core of two laws, one principle, and one norm. The same system appears in the natural sciences, philosophy, and engineering respectively as the “Factor Hierarchy System,” “Information Isomorphism Epistemology,” and the “Scientific Discovery Operating System.” The core work of this paper includes: integrating the functional complementarity, operational connection, and axiomatic structure of the two laws; unifying the core theorem system constituted by fifteen mathematical papers and one philosophical thematic paper; consolidating the verification results across six empirical disciplines, six theoretical demotions, and three tool replacements or extensions; and delineating the philosophical orientations and applicable boundaries of the system. This paper candidly declares: all verification comes from the same author’s series of preprints and has not yet undergone independent third-party replication; the verification levels across the six disciplines differ; at least seven mathematical papers contain substantive negative results; and all 81 open problems are detailed in the three mathematical series surveys.

Research Paradigm Statement: The core methodology, research direction, and final decisions were independently directed by the author. DeepSeek assisted with code implementation, data presentation, and text drafting. The author takes full academic responsibility for the final content.

title: Financial Adviser Histories, Firm Context, and the Allocation of Regulatory Attention
affiliations: and National University of Singapore (NUS) - NUS Business School

detail.title: Financial Adviser Histories, Firm Context, and the Allocation of Regulatory Attention

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Regulators cannot examine every financial adviser, so they need simple rules that turn public information into monitoring priorities. Using 2.7 million adviser-year observations, we study whether an adviser's current firm improves targeting beyond the adviser's own record. We develop a dynamic observed-state model that links adviser histories, firm assignment, new public-record risk, and employment transitions. We estimate the four state-contingent disclosure hazards freely. The estimates yield a strict ordering: prior records define broad risk tiers, while record-intensive firms identify higher-risk advisers within each tier. This ordering motivates a prospective monitoring rule that preserves priority by prior-record count and uses firm context only within a count tier. At a fixed 5 percent budget, the contextual rule captures 4.28 percent more subsequent disclosures than a record-count rule. Across the two headline outcomes, matching its capture would require the record-count rule to expand capacity by 7.4 to 9.9 percent. At the scale of FINRA's Member Supervision budget, this expansion corresponds to a $42-$57 million annual supervisory-capacity equivalent under proportional scaling.

title: Trade Policy Uncertainty Across Borders: Evidence from Local Projections and SVARs in the United States and China
affiliations: Texas Tech University and Texas Tech University

detail.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty Across Borders: Evidence from Local Projections and SVARs in the United States and China

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the domestic and international macroeconomic effects of trade policy uncertainty (TPU) shocks between the United States and China. While the domestic consequences of uncertainty are well documented, less is known about the bilateral transmission of trade policy uncertainty between the world's two largest economies. Using Structural Vector Autoregression (SVAR) and Local Projections (LP), this study estimates the dynamic responses of output, investment, consumption, international trade, interest rates, the real effective exchange rate, and financial markets to both domestic and foreign TPU shocks. The results reveal substantial international spillover effects that frequently match or exceed the corresponding domestic responses. U.S. TPU shocks generate significant and persistent declines in Chinese investment, trade, and financial market performance, while TPU shocks originating in China exert pronounced contractionary effects on U.S. investment, international trade, and financial markets. Financial markets and exchange rates respond almost immediately to uncertainty shocks, whereas real economic activity adjusts more gradually over subsequent quarters. These findings suggest that trade policy uncertainty propagates across borders through trade, financial, and exchange-rate channels, underscoring the importance of accounting for international spillovers when evaluating the macroeconomic consequences of trade policy uncertainty.

title: Periodic Adjustments — The Dialogue Continues
affiliations: University of Washington - School of Law and University of Michigan Law School

detail.title: Periodic Adjustments — The Dialogue Continues

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not Applicable
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract:
This article is a continuation of the ongoing dialogue that we have had with Michael McDonald concerning the cost sharing regulation, reg. section 1.482-7, and the application of periodic adjustments.

This article includes discussions of several subjects. These include:

First, it examines what is arm’s length pricing in the “commensurate with income” context. Its explanations provide an understanding of both the regulatory decision to make the ALP principle the standard, and importantly, the fact that what reg. sections 1.482-4(f )(2) and 1.482-7(i)(6) establish as pricing for any specific taxpayer situation is, by definition, an arm’s-length result.

Second, it discusses risk in the context of CWI.

Third, it discusses the history behind why we have the regulation allowing CSAs despite their use in the past several decades as a critical component and enabler of aggressive profit shifting structures.

title: Mathematical Foundations of the Information Isomorphism Law: A Complete Formalization of the Three Ontological Levels, Detection Sufficiency, and Exact Permutation Control

detail.title: Mathematical Foundations of the Information Isomorphism Law: A Complete Formalization of the Three Ontological Levels, Detection Sufficiency, and Exact Permutation Control

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract:
The Information Isomorphism Law (Tang, 2026ac) claims that in complex systems grounded in objective data and exhibiting regime switching, statistical structures carry information about regime structures. The law contains three progressive ontological levels—existence (information traces exist), correspondence (systematic correspondence exists between traces and regimes), and precision (encoding is precise on truth-known systems). This paper surveys the three papers of the mathematization series of the Information Isomorphism Law (Tang, 2026aq–2026as), and formally declares that the three levels have acquired complete mathematical foundations in the dimension of structural break detection.
The sufficiency direction is established in two steps: Tang (2026af) proves the Global Maximum Point Invariance Theorem in the linear model—the unified shape function attains a global unique maximum at the true boundary, and the standardized limits of Chow F/n, Wald*/n, and LR/n share this maximum point; Tang (2026aq) generalizes it to the L² function space, proving that the L² unified shape function attains a global unique maximum at the true boundary, that the multi-regime sufficiency theorem gives a global minimum of the functional-space BIC at the true boundary set, and that the spectral weighted sufficiency theorem establishes sufficiency uniformly over the entire spectral weighting family. The X-dependent convex combination lemma provides the geometric foundation for the multi-regime generalization; the detection information loss corollary and the detection resolution–information lower bound duality proposition quantitatively connect detection geometry with the estimation information limit.
The necessity direction is established by Tang (2026ar): under the null hypothesis, the unified shape function tends to zero in probability everywhere (at rate O_p(n^{-1} log n)); the finite-sample false-peak control theorem proves that the permutation test exactly controls the false positive rate; the extreme value limit theorem proves that the standardized statistic converges to the Brownian-bridge supremum distribution (aligned with Andrews, 1993); the permutation test power theorem and the local power theorem complete the full characterization under the alternative.
The bijection is completed by Tang (2026as) through the conjunction: a regime switch exists if and only if the population unified shape function attains a global unique maximum; the Local Bijection Theorem, based on the one-sided kernel locally weighted unified shape function, generalizes this to a pointwise correspondence in the multi-regime model; and the pseudo-peak phenomenon proposition of global splitting establishes the necessity of localization through an explicit counterexample.
This paper gives a Preliminary Establishment Statement: in the statistical dimension of structural break detection, the three ontological levels of the Information Isomorphism Law have all been mathematically formalized, and the conjunction of the sufficiency and necessity directions constitutes the bijection theorem. This paper provides a cross-disciplinary verification matrix that maps the sufficiency and necessity directions to empirical findings in six disciplines—finance, astronomy, statistical physics, particle physics, chemistry, and nuclear physics; consolidates open problems IIL-T1 to IIL-T22; and provides a concrete tool list for subsequent research. Together with the Switch Measure Theory survey (Tang, 2026al) and the Factor Hierarchy Law mathematization survey (Tang, 2026ap), this paper constitutes the complete survey of the three mathematical series of the Factor Hierarchy framework.
Research Paradigm Statement: The core methodology, research direction, and final decisions were independently directed by the author. DeepSeek assisted with code implementation, data presentation, and text drafting. The author takes full academic responsibility for the final content.

title: What's the Use of the Patent Strict Utility Requirement?

detail.title: What's the Use of the Patent Strict Utility Requirement?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: No outside funding.

detail.abstract: The current interpretation of patent utility prohibits patents on inventions that do not have a known use to members of the public such as consumers or patients. This Article makes two contributions. First, the Article shows that the current interpretation of utility arose from an unproven, and probably incorrect, assumption of unduly high transaction costs of licensing patents on inventions of unknown end-user utility (research intermediaries). The Article examines the history of patent utility in the U.S. and shows that the current interpretation of utility arose not from empirical study or the recognition of significant problems arising under the historic standard. Rather, the Patent Office, and then the Supreme Court, seem to have simply assumed that transaction costs would be high, that thickets and hold-ups would result, and that downstream research would be significantly impeded. This assumption may have been reasonable at the time (although several dissenting judges disagreed), but it seems increasingly unsupported given history and experience showing how adept markets are at clearing IP rights in crowded fields. The second contribution of the Article shows that the thicket/hold-up problem is likely to be less severe for research intermediaries than for other types of inventions, such as high-tech inventions. Thickets and hold-ups are most likely to occur in vertical supply chains with many patent owners, or in cases in which many inventions must be combined to produce a single product. This is the well-known “double marginalization,” or “successive monopoly,” problem. The Article shows that given the economic realities of research and development (R&D) involving inventions with unknown end-user utility, the double marginalization problem is less likely to occur because the economic incentives around patented research intermediaries will result in joint-venture approaches rather than successive monopolization.

title: Role-Playing Games for Building Resilience to Influence Operations Targeting the Research Workforce
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Independent and University of Illinois

detail.title: Role-Playing Games for Building Resilience to Influence Operations Targeting the Research Workforce

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no personal or financial relationships with people or organizations that may have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was funded by the National Science Foundation.

detail.abstract:
Adversaries increasingly target researchers directly by cultivating relationships, exploiting prestige and the pressure to publish, and obtaining sensitive details through what looks like ordinary academic contact. This is in part a cognitive security problem: the vulnerability lies in how researchers interpret relationships, obligations, and routine requests. 

We present a collaborative tabletop role-playing method, adapted from improvisational story games, for modeling influence operations that target researchers. Rather than scripting a scenario for participants to solve, as traditional wargames or tabletop exercises do, our method asks mixed-role groups to improvise how pressure, ambition, and trust compound into compromise. Gameplay surfaces behavioral indicators and decision points that checklists overlook. 

The method is intended to complement disclosure rules and export controls. We argue that improvisational role play is a practical way to build cognitive-security skills in the researcher workforce. The Cognitive Dimension of Research Security When a nation-state or commercial competitor wants access to cutting-edge research, the most direct route might be ordinary interaction with a researcher. The use of ostensibly legitimate interactions to discern sensitive information is well documented. Tom Clancy famously

title: From Waste to Watts and Water: A Climate-Responsive Framework for Air-Conditioning Condensate Recovery, Condenser Pre-Cooling and Urban Resource Conservation in Bangladesh

detail.title: From Waste to Watts and Water: A Climate-Responsive Framework for Air-Conditioning Condensate Recovery, Condenser Pre-Cooling and Urban Resource Conservation in Bangladesh

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. This research received no external funding.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animal subjects. Therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Air-conditioning systems remove moisture from indoor air and commonly discharge the resulting condensate without beneficial use. This study develops the Waste-to-Watts-and-Water (WWW) Framework, a model-based feasibility approach that integrates condensate recovery, humidity-responsive condenser-air pre-cooling, surplus-water reuse, auxiliary-energy accounting, and scenario-based techno-economic assessment for Dhaka, Bangladesh. A literature-calibrated seasonal model was applied to representative pre-monsoon, monsoon and post-monsoon conditions, with season-specific evaporative effectiveness derived transparently from a psychrometric wet-bulb-depression calculation rather than assumed independently for each season. The central case yields gross air-conditioning energy reductions of 8.0%, 1.0% and 3.5% in the three respective periods; more optimistic values of 11.38%, 2.10% and 5.42%, corresponding to a higher assumed evaporative effectiveness, are retained as an upper-performance case. For a representative 5-ton-equivalent commercial unit operating 1,820 hours annually, the central model estimates 317.72 kWh/year of gross air-conditioning energy reduction. After deducting 32.37 kWh/year for pump, UV-treatment and controller electricity, the estimated net reduction is 285.35 kWh/year, equivalent to approximately BDT 4,423 at an assumed tariff of BDT 15.50/kWh. After non-electric operating costs, estimated annual cash flow is BDT 3,373, with a simple payback of 4.03 years. A preliminary, non-instrumented field observation of condensate generation from a single 2-ton unit over 40 sessions (Appendix B) is broadly consistent with, though somewhat lower than, the water-generation assumption adopted in the central model. An illustrative deployment scenario of 150,000 units, checked for order-of-magnitude plausibility against national air-conditioning market data rather than treated as an arbitrary figure, yields approximately 42.80 GWh/year of net grid-energy reduction and 2.40 billion L/year of surplus-condensate recovery. These outputs are model-based projections rather than measured outcomes or a verified equipment inventory; instrumented field testing, summarised in the validation protocol in Appendix A, is required before performance, public-health, corrosion or city-scale benefits can be confirmed.

title: Dealer Risk Management of Digital Options: Call Spread Smoothing versus Displacement under Execution Costs and Jump Risk
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Dealer Risk Management of Digital Options: Call Spread Smoothing versus Displacement under Execution Costs and Jump Risk

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interests to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Self. No external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper compares two approaches used in practice by Dealers to manage the risk of digital options: smoothing hedge sensitivity around the contractual strike via a finite-width call spread, and moving the critical region away from the contractual strike via a displaced digital. The analysis bases this comparison on the consequences of the dynamic hedging paths generated by each representation, the resulting hedge P&L, execution cost and management loss, the potential for pre-expiry unwind and client monetization of digital options, and the influence of those factors in determining the relative performance of the two representations under both continuous dynamics and discontinuous spot moves. Across both the continuous and jump-diffusion experiments, the call spread produces lower average management loss in the overwhelming majority of the tested cases. The displaced digital becomes competitive only in an extremely narrow set of conditions, concentrated at the largest payout sizes and, under continuous diffusion, the highest assumed client unwind probabilities, where lower execution costs affect the overall result. Even in those cases, the displaced digital has higher management loss than the call spread at the 95th and 99th percentiles in every comparison, showing that its occasional advantage in average management loss does not extend to the upper end of the loss distribution. Introducing jumps makes the displaced digital less competitive as jump probability increases. Finally, when the call spread bend and displaced digital shift are selected separately to minimise the average management loss of each representation, the call spread has lower average management loss in every comparison under both spot processes. Collectively, the results overwhelmingly favour call spread smoothing as the more effective hedge representation across the conditions tested.

title: The Unpriced Cost of Replication: Evidential Fragility and the Allocation of Verification Effort

detail.title: The Unpriced Cost of Replication: Evidential Fragility and the Allocation of Verification Effort

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it relies exclusively on publicly available secondary data and involves no new data collection from human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was obtained for this work.

detail.abstract: Replication projects can report high power while allocating no additional observations to the most uncertain original findings. We audit this allocation using 248 claims from the SCORE project and an uncertainty-aware safeguard benchmark defined for 246 claims. Among new-data replications, the median safeguard target was 2.04 times the standard power target calculated from the original point estimate, and 20.3% of claims fell short. The most-fragile tercile accounted for 4,812 of the 5,337 observations in the benchmark shortfall. Conditional on the conventional target, realized sample size showed no positive response to the safeguard markup and rejected the unit elasticity implied by proportional adjustment. High nominal power therefore did not translate into greater verification effort where original evidence was most uncertain. We recommend reporting conventional and uncertainty-adjusted targets alongside the constraint or judgment determining the final sample.

title: Smart Money or Costly Folklore? A Systematic Evaluation of ICT/Smart-Money-Concepts Trading Rules in G10 FX
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Smart Money or Costly Folklore? A Systematic Evaluation of ICT/Smart-Money-Concepts Trading Rules in G10 FX

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. No personal or financial relationship with any person or organization influenced the design, execution, or reporting of this research. All data were sourced from a retail brokerage feed under the author's own account; the author holds no undisclosed position, sponsorship, or compensation arrangement related to the instruments, strategies, or methods discussed in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was self-funded and conducted independently by the author, with no grant, institutional, or corporate sponsorship.

detail.abstract: "ICT" (Inner Circle Trader) and "Smart Money Concepts" (SMC) denote a body of retail trading-education content — built and disseminated almost entirely through YouTube and social media, not peer review — that claims to describe how large institutional participants engineer price action in liquid markets: they sweep resting stop-loss orders at obvious technical levels ("liquidity"), reveal their true intent through abrupt shifts in short-term market structure ("Change of Character," CHoCH), and leave "Fair Value Gaps" (FVG) — untraded price voids left by displacement candles — that price is said to revisit before continuing. This paper subjects six mechanically well-defined, independently designed trading rules drawn from this tradition to this project's full walk-forward, bootstrap, permutation, and holdout evaluation protocol on EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, and USDJPY across intraday timeframes. We find no evidence that ICT/SMC concepts work as literally taught. We do find something more interesting: three independently constructed liquidity-sweep mechanisms — built around swing-based equal highs/lows, real order blocks, and Asian session ranges — unanimously agree, across 65 of 66 combined fold-selections, that a swept level predicts continuation, not the textbook reversal. A fourth mechanism (Change of Character confirmed by a Fair Value Gap retracement) unanimously finds the opposite type of error: the textbook reversal read should be faded, not traded. One flagship result — EURUSD H1 CHoCH+FVG, faded — clears significance (p = 0.0192), sits inside this project's acceptable walk-forward-efficiency band (1.58), and its holdout agrees in sign and magnitude (+19.3% return, 60 trades, profit factor 1.50); a companion Monte Carlo diagnostic places its combined expectancy at roughly the 81st percentile of its own long-run bootstrap distribution — respectable, not a lucky draw. A second result (AUDUSD H1, same setup) is more significant (p = 0.0074) but its walk-forward efficiency (2.08) and its 97th-percentile placement in the same bootstrap exercise together mark it as the more fragile of the two. We also report two negative results with independent value: a genuine transaction-cost-economics finding, in which a strategy's real R-multiple edge is shown to be smaller than the fixed per-lot commission it forces through oversized, tight-stop position sizing (repaired by a simple minimum-stop-distance floor); and a validation-methodology case study, in which a real implementation bug in an order-block detector — invisible to every statistical gate this project runs — was caught only by a human looking at a chart. Channel and trendline trading, tested as a free-direction negative control, provides the one case in this paper's history where fixing an assumed direction removes catastrophic failure without revealing any real edge, and does so with no coherent economic story behind the winning sign — the appropriate contrast case to the paper's three positive continuation findings and one positive fade finding, all of which do carry such a story. Two robustness checks probe the flagship result directly: recomputing the Deflated Sharpe Ratio across a range of plausible trial counts shows both EURUSD H1 and AUDUSD H1 fail this gate at every defensible count (unlike a case reported in Paper 2 of this series, where a different result's DSR verdict flips depending on this exact choice), confirming rather than complicating the paper's decision to rest validation on other evidence; and a minimum-detectable-effect calculation on Study 5's frequency-fix shows the original 33-trade sample was mechanically underpowered relative to its own point estimate, while the improved 48-trade version is not — a quantitative account of why more, differently composed data, not merely a bigger effect, is what crossed the significance threshold.

title: DOES INVESTOR ATTENTION PRECEDE ADVERSE OUTCOMES? EVIDENCE FROM THE BRAZILIAN STOCK MARKET

detail.title: DOES INVESTOR ATTENTION PRECEDE ADVERSE OUTCOMES? EVIDENCE FROM THE BRAZILIAN STOCK MARKET

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Between 2020 and 2026, five companies listed on the B3 stock exchange entered judicial recovery (bankruptcy protection). All of them were, in the preceding years, in the group of stocks that attracted the most market attention. This article examines whether this coincidence is systematic-and finds, along the way, an asymmetry that the attention literature had not reported. Covering all spot market trades between January 2, 2020, and September 4, 2026, we identify 3,211 attention events across 232 stocks, defined by abnormal financial volume, and estimate abnormal returns using a market model. The mean cumulative abnormal return is positive and significant over long horizons-73.01% in one year (t = 2.90). The median is negative across all examined windows, reaching-10.57%, and only 45.8% of events yield a positive abnormal return (z =-4.78). The mean and median point in opposite directions, and this divergence is precisely the finding. The typical stock going through an attention peak underperforms the market; a minority produces extreme gains that dominate the mean. Instances of extraordinary appreciation that populate the news and investors' memories exist and are verifiable-but they are the tail of a distribution whose center is negative. The availability heuristic, when applied to this distribution, produces a biased estimate of the probability of success based on real cases, making the behavior resistant to experience. Regarding terminal outcomes: stocks in the upper tercile of attention event frequency between 2020 and 2022 recorded, in the subsequent period, a 5.0% rate of entry into judicial recovery, compared to 0.0% in the lower tercile, and a median return of-5.0%, against +11.2%. A logistic model confirms the association with severe deterioration (z = 3.48), unexplainable by stock size. The pattern survives temporal separation between attention measurement and outcome observation, as well as the exclusion of attention generated by stocks already collapsing. For the individual investor, whose buying behavior the literature links to asset visibility, this means that their decision criterion is associated, in the examined sample, with inferior median performance and a higher incidence of adverse terminal outcomes.

title: Patent Protection for Genetic Innovation: Monsanto and Myriad

detail.title: Patent Protection for Genetic Innovation: Monsanto and Myriad

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Cato paid a $1,000 honorarium for presenting the article at its annual Constitution Day Conference.

detail.abstract:
Genetic science is increasingly important to the economy and people's individual lives. Among other things, genetic scientists have contributed to the ongoing Green Revolution that began in the 1950s and continues making agriculture ever more efficient. The study of genetics can also inform people about their risks for disease and develop therapies to treat many of the health scourges of our time. Of course, the genetic research that brings forth such advances (or sometimes endangers our health, according to some critics of genetically modified organisms (GMO)) is complex and costly to conduct. Thus, since at least the 1980s, companies have turned to patents to protect their innovations in genetics. 

This term, the Supreme Court ruled on two cases involving patents in the field of genetics. In the first case, the Court upheld a decision preventing a farmer from reproducing Monsanto's Roundup Ready soybeans for subsequent plantings. In the second case, the Court ruled that natural DNA, as it exists in living organisms, is not patentable, but that complementary DNA ("cDNA"), which is produced in laboratories, is patentable even though cDNA is very similar to DNA. 

In practical effect, this term the Court maintained protection for genetic crop modifications that are passed on in successive generations of the plants ("self-replicating" genetically modified plants). In disallowing patents on DNA but allowing them on cDNA, the Court decreased the patent rights given to researchers who discover genetic mutations that correlate with disease, but did not fully eliminate them. As to the effects on substantive patent law, the Court explained that the legal doctrine of patent exhaustion does not operate to permit the "making" of new copies of a patented genetic seed, even if the method of making the new copy is merely planting the patented seed and letting it grow more seeds that contain the patented genetic trait. The Court also continued to grapple with one of the most amorphous and intellectually unsatisfying areas in patent law—the question of what types of innovation and discovery should qualify for patentability. The Court has not clearly stated a uniform statutory interpretation and policy rationale for what should be patentable, and thus continues to make piecemeal decisions in individual cases without providing clear guidelines or predictability in this area of law. Notwithstanding that, this term the Court probably arrived at a decision that is good policy when it comes to patents ongenetic material that occurs in nature.

title:
Trial by ICE: Immigration Detention as

Adjudication and the “Great Writ” of

Habeas Corpus
affiliations: UC Law, San Francisco

detail.title:
Trial by ICE: Immigration Detention as

Adjudication and the “Great Writ” of

Habeas Corpus

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.ethicsApproval: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract:
In immigration law, detention has replaced adjudication as the

executive’s de facto tool for resolving removal cases. Detention

accelerates proceedings, pressures immigrants to abandon claims,

and helps the government obtain outcomes that would be costly and

time-consuming to secure through adjudication. This transformation

has sidelined immigration court, once the central site of decision-

making. In its place, detention has become supreme.

This Article argues that as the executive has expanded its use of

detention, detention has taken on adjudicatory functions, a

phenomenon that this Article calls “detention as adjudication.”

“Detention as adjudication” refers to a strategic effort to use

detention to pressure immigrants to give up their legal efforts to fight

removal. As a result of this shift, habeas corpus has moved from the

margins of immigration law to its center. District courts, long stripped

of jurisdiction over immigration cases, have taken on a new role

because of the use of detention. These federal courts are now the forum

in which immigrants obtain bond hearings, challenge unexplained

redetention, and enforce limits on civil custody.

This Article draws on the explosion of recent habeas cases,

unprecedented in modern times, and on the author’s experience

litigating these cases in four federal districts. It advances three main

claims: Detention is now the executive’s primary tool for deciding

immigration cases; habeas has become an ordinary—and, indeed,

indispensable—mechanism for enforcing immigration law even in

routine cases; and habeas has emerged as continuity-enforcing

doctrine, bridging the divide between this administration and the ones

that preceded it. Immigration habeas, the Article concludes, is not an

anomaly. It is the law of immigration as it is now practiced.

title:
U.S. Financial Uncertainty and Emerging-Market Vulnerability:
Evidence from SVAR and Two-Country DSGE Models
affiliations: Texas Tech University

detail.title:
U.S. Financial Uncertainty and Emerging-Market Vulnerability:
Evidence from SVAR and Two-Country DSGE Models

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the transmission of U.S. financial uncertainty to Mexico, modeled as a representative small open emerging economy. First, using U.S.-Mexico data, I estimate a Structural Vector Autoregression (SVAR) to establish the empirical effects of a U.S. financial uncertainty shock. The results show a flight-to-safety episode characterized by declines in Mexican equity prices, currency depreciation, and a persistent contraction in economic activity. Second, I develop a non-linear two-country New Keynesian DSGE model, calibrated to U.S.-Mexico data, to explain the mechanisms underlying these empirical responses. The model incorporates an endogenous sovereign risk premium, nominal rigidities, and investment adjustment costs and is consistent with the main empirical responses observed in the SVAR, while providing a structural interpretation of the mechanisms driving them. Counterfactual exercises identify these features as important transmission mechanisms and show that greater trade dependence amplifies the effects of foreign uncertainty through exchange-rate pass-through and imported inflation. The analysis also reveals a policy trade-off: a more aggressive monetary response better stabilizes inflation and exchange-rate dynamics but at the cost of tighter financial conditions, lower asset valuations, and weaker real activity. Overall, the findings highlight the joint role of financial frictions, trade exposure, and monetary policy in shaping emerging-market vulnerability to external financial shocks.

title: Role-Playing Games for Building Resilience to Influence Operations Targeting the Research Workforce

detail.abstract:
Adversaries increasingly target researchers directly by cultivating relationships, exploiting prestige and the pressure to publish, and obtaining sensitive details through what looks like ordinary academic contact. This is in part a cognitive security problem: the vulnerability lies in how researchers interpret relationships, obligations, and routine requests.

We present a collaborative tabletop role-playing method, adapted from improvisational story games, for modeling influence operations that target researchers. Rather than scripting a scenario for participants to solve, as traditional wargames or tabletop exercises do, our method asks mixed-role groups to improvise how pressure, ambition, and trust compound into compromise. Gameplay surfaces behavioral indicators and decision points that checklists overlook.

The method is intended to complement disclosure rules and export controls. We argue that improvisational role play is a practical way to build cognitive-security skills in the researcher workforce.

title: Kinetopus Engine: A Parsimonious Physical-Mathematical Pipeline for Local-First Financial Time Series Forecasting using Sparse Identification of Dynamical Systems (SINDy)

detail.abstract: Financial time series analysis has long been trapped in a dichotomy between linear, oversimplified statistical models (e.g., ARIMA) and opaque, computationally expensive deep learning black boxes (e.g., LSTMs, Transformers). This paper introduces Kinetopus Engine, a parsimonious, White-Box Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) framework that challenges the assumption of pure stochastic randomness by constructing a mathematically justified continuous physical perspective over discrete financial data. Operating under low computational complexity on consumer-grade CPU hardware (≤ 16 GB RAM), the pipeline integrates five core stages: (1) Spectral sensing via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to detect dominant cyclical frequencies; (2) Topological manifold smoothing via C 2 Splines to reconstruct continuous price-volume trajectories; (3) Online Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) control mechanisms for real-time structural regime-shift slicing; (4) Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) to discover explicit, parsimonious ordinary differential equations dr/dt = f (r, V); and (5) Probabilistic Monte Carlo trajectory projection via Euler-Maruyama stochastic differential equations (SDEs) stabilized by a hydrodynamic friction regularizer (λ = 0.99). Empirical evaluation through an extensive walk-forward benchmark encompassing 3,525 evaluation iterations across a heterogeneous six-asset universe (BTC-USD, ETH-USD, MSFT, QQQ, XLF, GLD) demonstrates a sustained aggregate directional Hit Ratio of 59.15% at a 150-candle horizon (∼ 7.5 months), achieving strong statistical significance against a random-walk null hypothesis (z = 4.942, p < 0.0001) and peaking at 71.57% on broadmarket index equities (QQQ) and 70.30% on technology equities (MSFT). Furthermore, the physical engine operates at sub-millisecond CPU latency (< 1 ms per episode, ∼ 1, 525× faster than an LSTM baseline) with a 98.60% mathematical validity rate, delivering full phase-space interpretability and generating explicit, inspectable governing equations. A complete, interactive deployment is made openly accessible on Hugging Face Spaces.

detail.abstract: The introduction discusses the long-standing 'nature versus nurture' debate and clarifies that this is now outdated; a more integrative approach is currently favoured, centred on the notion that both genetic and environmental factors contribute to the origins of antisocial behaviour-this understanding has been informed by studies of twins and adopted children, and, more recently, studies that also utilise molecular genetics to identify the genes responsible. Throughout the paper, some of these studies are critically reviewed in order to clarify what proportion of the variance is explained by genetic factors and what proportion by environmental factors, as well as which genes are the strongest candidates for being responsible for antisocial behaviour; one of the genes for which there is the most evidence is the low-activity MAOA gene. The paper also addresses differences in brain function and structure among individuals exhibiting a pattern of antisocial behaviour, how these relate to behavioural and personality changes in these individuals, as well as the possible influence of certain genes (such as MAOA) on these brain changes.

detail.abstract: For more than four decades, the 60/40 stock/bond portfolio has served as a benchmark for delivering reasonable returns without excessive risk. More recently, a 50/30/20 stock/bond/alternative portfolio has been suggested. We use gold as the alternative and as an inflation hedge. In this paper we ask: how much improvement over these benchmark fixed-weight portfolios can be obtained using widely available public data and standard methods from quantitative finance? We restrict ourselves to long-only dynamic portfolios of stocks, bonds, and gold, plus cash, rebalancing monthly, using only publicly available data. We evaluate portfolios on the conventional metrics: return, volatility, Sharpe ratio (computed in excess of the federal funds rate), drawdown, and turnover, in addition to consistency of performance over time, judged by the consistency of the realized annual volatility. Over the 20–year period 2006–2026, using a conservative estimate of trading costs, we show that all risk-adjusted and drawdown metrics are improved using simple volatility control, where we dynamically mix the fixed-weight portfolios with cash so as to target a fixed volatility. This method relies on a simple estimate of portfolio volatility derived from past returns. We also demonstrate that more sophisticated portfolios based on convex optimization—similar to those used in quantitative hedge funds— yield further substantial improvement in return and risk-adjusted return. We consider two such portfolios, one that uses a simple estimate of future returns based on past returns, and one that forecasts future returns based on past returns and just a handful of widely available public economic data. These portfolios also outperform a suite of standard risk-based allocation methods, such as risk parity and minimum variance, evaluated on the same assets and data. Our paper is accompanied by open-source software that implements the methods and replicates all results.

detail.abstract: This note examines Greece's low private-pension penetration and persistent trust deficit through a structured comparison with two differently institutionalized markets: Belarus, a state-dominated system with a legally constrained product architecture, and Poland, a fellow EU/Solvency II jurisdiction with materially more developed funded pension structures. Rather than treating the three countries symmetrically, the analysis is organized around what each comparator tests for the Greek case, examined along three dimensions — participation mechanisms, product architecture, and bancassurance distribution. Poland's auto-enrollment third-pillar scheme (PPK) raised participation from roughly one in two eligible workers to nearly two in three within about 19 months, offering a tested design alternative for Greece's own 2026 reform process; Greece's unit-linked life segment appears larger in relative terms than Poland's, reversing an initial assumption about which country should benchmark which; and a prospective natural-experiment setting in the Greek market — Piraeus Bank's November 2025 acquisition of Ethniki Insurance, alongside NN Hellas's pre-existing bancassurance partnership with the same bank — offers an unusually clean quasi-experimental opportunity to test the distinction between affiliate-synergy and organic trust-transfer mechanisms in bancassurance distribution once outcome data exist, a distinction that Belarus's practitioner-reviewed data first identified as analytically necessary. All primary findings are sourced directly from national supervisory and industry-association bulletins and, where relevant, reviewed with in-market practitioners; remaining limitations are classified by cause — recency, statutory access restriction, disclosure granularity, or cross-country denominator comparability — rather than treated as undifferentiated unfinished research.

detail.abstract: In 303 Creative LLC v. Elenis, the Supreme Court ruled in favor of a web designer who refused to create wedding websites for same-sex couples. We examine the effects of this decision through a field experiment in the wedding web design industry. We find that exposure to the decision reduced designers' response rates to all couples, with interracial couples experiencing an additional significant penalty. detail.abstract: Mobile learning technologies (MLTs) have been on the rise in both higher education and organisational settings, but progress in implementing them within organisations has been uneven. While there is evidence base for psychological predictors of acceptance across the globe, primarily through the Technology Acceptance Model, Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, and Theory of Planned Behaviour, these models and theories have limited contextual applicability in South African higher education (SAHE). The review followed PRISMA-ScR guidance. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, PsycINFO, and ERIC for studies published between 2019 and 2025. The synthesis suggests that acceptance is consistently related to perceived usefulness or performance expectancy, perceived ease of use or effort expectancy, self-efficacy, and social influence. These predictors, however, are more strongly moderated by perceived behavioural control, facilitating conditions, anxiety, and trust in SAHE, reflecting infrastructural constraints, workload pressures, and digital inequality. The review concludes that, although dominant acceptance models remain theoretically sound, they need to be applied in the context of SAHE, with a focus on institutional-level interventions. This implies that MLTs are best used as integrated resources rather than as complete replacements for traditional teaching, and that platforms with lower friction are more acceptable to employees.

detail.abstract: A companion article, the Rebound Test against J-space (Magni, 2026c), proposed that Complementary Semantics' claim should be broadened from the euphemism-specific case to a fully general one: every common noun's complementary affordances defocus into the Umbra Cone regardless of evaluative charge, with the euphemism-specific case demoted to a special instance of the general one. That conclusion rested on a small, four-domain item bank without a direct statistical contrast between neutral affordance pairs and pairs of mere association. This article reports a properly powered re-test of that broader claim, ten item pairs per condition (evaluative, neutral affordance, mere co-occurrence) with three sentence templates each, ninety base-rebound comparisons in total. The general claim does not survive the re-test: neutral affordance pairs are statistically indistinguishable from mere co-occurrence, while evaluative pairs alone produce a strong, Bonferroni-significant effect, in the direction opposite to the one the rebound mechanism predicted. A revised H1 (corpus dominance) finds no relationship; a revised H2 (independently normed affective valence) predicts rebound magnitude significantly across all thirty pairs; a revised H3 shows that evaluative-versus-neutral category, not a continuous cost measure, carries the explanatory weight. Read together, these results argue for retracting Complementary Semantics' general, motivation-indifferent claim and restating it as affect-gated: structural coexistence of complementary affordances is necessary but not sufficient for the Umbra Cone dynamic, which activates in proportion to affective charge. This revision brings the mechanism back inside the Theory's own vocabulary of prepositional focusing and defocusing, in preference to the borrowed ironic-process account, and converges 1 with unpublished work on a Law of Generation for the Umbra Cone (Magni & Marchetti, in preparation), which independently proposes a threshold condition for when a cone forms at all.

detail.abstract: Complementary Semantics, the claim within Learnable Theory that a noun's unselected affordances recede into a zone of reduced activation, the Umbra Cone, rather than disappearing, has moved through three empirical tests before the one reported here. Shining Shadows (Magni, 2026a) proposed three falsifiable hypotheses for the construct. Measuring the Umbra Cone (Magni, 2026b) found the proposed instrument, a logit-lens probe, too fragile to test them, and validated a concept-direction alternative instead. The Rebound Test against J-space (Magni, 2026c) added a minimizing-clause manipulation that distinguished genuinely complementary pairs from mere textual association, then used that result to propose a broadened, motivationindifferent version of the claim: that every noun's complementary affordances defocus regardless of evaluative charge. Below the Threshold (Magni, 2026d) re-tested that broadening at a larger, properly powered scale and found it did not survive; affectively neutral affordances proved statistically indistinguishable from mere co-occurrence, while affective charge, measured against independently collected human norms, predicted rebound magnitude significantly across every condition tested. Complementary Semantics was accordingly restated as affect-gated rather than structurally universal: the coexistence of complementary affordances is necessary but not sufficient, and the Umbra Cone dynamic activates only in proportion to affective charge. That restatement left one question open, whether the charge-rebound relationship it rests on is linear across its full range or whether it saturates or reverses at extreme charge, a third regime distinct from ordinary affect-gated defocusing that would matter directly for attempts 1 elsewhere in this research program to reconcile the Umbra Cone with the Jungian shadow. This article reports a preregistered test of that question. Forty euphemism-dysphemism and neutralaffordance pairs, spanning four affective-charge bands from near zero to extreme, were run through three GPT-2 models of increasing scale using the concept-direction and rebound method validated in the two preceding articles. Two methodological problems were identified and corrected before any hypothesis test was run: a sentence-length dilution artifact in meanpooled hidden states, and an unintended confound between affective charge and phrase length in the item bank itself. In two sentences, the result: a curvilinear relationship was rejected at every model scale, in every one of one hundred twenty leave-one-out refits, and in every bootstrap interval, with no exception anywhere in the data, so the specific empirical grounding a three-regime reconciliation with the Jungian shadow would need is not supported; a linear relationship, the affect-gated mechanism itself, was in the same data confirmed at medium and large scale and left fragile rather than refuted at small scale, meaning the account established in Below the Threshold is reinforced by a harder test, not merely left standing.

detail.abstract: Mortgage repayments make up 30% of Euro-area household saving flows. I show that fixed amortization schedules, prevalent in European mortgage markets, induce wealth accumulation through debt repayment but limit consumption smoothing. In a life-cycle model with uninsurable income risk and illiquid home equity, costly deviation from scheduled repayment forces constrained homeowners to cut consumption and liquid saving. In the data, homebuyers are constrained, starting with little cash after home purchases; they save more than renters (including debt repayment) but accumulate less liquid wealth. I exploit a 2013 Dutch policy change that made previously-free flexible repayment costly through tax incentives. Homebuyers accelerated repayment and built less liquid buffers. The model matches these patterns and shows mandatory amortization increases the share of hand-to-mouth households by 15 percentage points, amplifying financial wealth inequality. Welfare losses, at 2-3% of lifetime consumption for the average homeowner, are equivalent to working an extra year before retirement.

title:
From Means of Payment to Settlement Asset: 
The Danger Stablecoins Pose to the European Economic Area and the Response of the EU and the ECB

detail.title:
From Means of Payment to Settlement Asset: 
The Danger Stablecoins Pose to the European Economic Area and the Response of the EU and the ECB

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No one influenced this study

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the danger that arises for the European Economic Area when
a dollar-pegged stablecoin migrates from the payment layer, where it is a claim
redeemable at any time, into the settlement layer, where obligations are finally
discharged. It combines the monetary theory of currency competition and
dollarization with the supervisory law of the Union and the United States (MiCAR,
GENIUS Act), with market data as of September 2026, and with a stylized quantity
model calibrated to euro-area aggregates for July 2026.
As long as the token remains redeemable, its effect on the price level is bounded
and the ECB's ability to steer it is preserved—at the cost of weaker transmission
and a more volatile funding base for banks. Acceptance in settlement removes the
redemption obligation: the issuer can create credit without a license and without
capital; the price level loses its anchor; and for a dollar token, currency substitution
takes the place of inflation, with the price level of the tokenized part of the economy
following American prices and the exchange rate. In the numerical example, a euro
coin of EUR 500 billion raises payment capacity by up to 2.8 percent on a one-off
basis and reduces banks' lending capacity by one to two percent; with settlement
acceptance and a reserve ratio of 20 percent the effect rises to 11.4 percent. Actual
data for 2015–2025 show that a dollar price level measured in euro would have
risen by 21 percent in 2022 alone, against 8.4 percent for the HICP.
The EU and the ECB have already built the defenses of the settlement side—
means-of-exchange thresholds, the interest prohibition, reserve rules, Pontes, the
digital euro, the ESRB recommendation. The danger now lies in the 2026 MiCAR
review, in multi-issuance, and in the time until 2029. The author recommends nine measures, first among them a rule of Union law that taxes, bank liabilities, and finality can be discharged in euro alone

detail.abstract:
Cambodia's KHQR, the national EMVCo-based payment QR operated on the National Bank of Cambodia's Bakong system, has been adopted widely enough that the public now treats any QR code as a payment instrument and extends to it the trust it holds in the central bank. Attackers exploit this in two ways that are routinely conflated: forgery, where a code is not what it claims to be, and deception, where a genuine code, correctly signed and payable to a correctly registered account, is presented under a false pretext.

This paper reports QRSeal, a project in two halves. KH-SQR is a signature specification for payment codes and document credentials, with an MIT-licensed reference implementation and a language-neutral conformance suite of fifty cases, thirty-eight of them negative. S0–S6 are institutional proposals, numbered rather than named because they are reference designs and not evaluated interventions. Neither is a standard: KH-SQR is proposed here, not adopted anywhere, and nothing in it is issued by or agreed with any Cambodian authority.

We use the artefact as evidence for a claim about where its own assurance stops. Inside a conforming verifier on an uncompromised device, a signature closes forgery; it does not touch deception, because a control enforced at one layer does not govern meaning created at the layer above it. Signing the code secures the instrument and cannot secure the transaction. A signature is also a provenance instrument, so what it asks a verifier to act on is the absence of one, which carries no information until coverage is near-complete; we report that a national scheme in Japan reached the same overlay attack and answered it with mandated visual uniformity for printed codes, an option compatible with the stall that has no device and one we had missed.

The corollary is constructive. Where a control cannot be enforced below the harm, four moves remain: raise the control above the meaning, reverse the transfer, remove the convertibility of the proceeds, or reallocate the loss. S0–S6 are one concrete instance of each move, sequenced so that a government could evaluate them in order, and not a costed programme; the first is a categorical prohibition on URL-bearing payment and official codes, which closes one channel and does not reduce the adversary's budget. We report two failures of our own work — the reference deployment does not meet its mirror-independence requirement, and the first container encoding was not readable by a conforming EMVCo parser, since corrected at a cost of sixty-one characters and one symbol version — and we treat the absence of Cambodia-specific incident data as a finding. The trajectory of exposure is argued from structure and not measured: a code that visibly verifies manufactures the confidence the unaddressed attack depends on, and nothing here has been deployed or trialled.

detail.abstract: The 'New Washington Consensus' (NWC) represents a major intellectual shift in the US approach to global economic governance. However, the NWC has never been subject to systematic academic critique. With Trump's return to the White House ushering in a new era of US trade policy, the NWC is widely considered to be politically irrelevant in the existing literature. This article provides one of the first sustained critical assessments of the NWC and its legacy for the future of the international economic order. In particular, it argues that, contrary to prevailing assumptions, it is too early to dismiss the NWC as intellectually defunct. Although some elements of the NWC have been criticised and subsequently discarded in the Trump 2.0 era, the NWC nonetheless established the intellectual framework for Trump 2.0's trade statecraft. Therefore, a more rigorous engagement with the NWC and its evolving legacy provides a useful lens for imagining the future of the international economic order.

title: The Rise of the U.S. Investor State: State Capitalist Impulses under Changing Global Political Economy

detail.title: The Rise of the U.S. Investor State: State Capitalist Impulses under Changing Global Political Economy

detail.abstract: While scholars conceptualized the expansion of state capital into private firms in China as an idiosyncratic form of political economy, called the 'Investor State' or 'Party-State Capitalism,' the high-profile federal equity investments under Trump 2.0 have led commentators to speculate about the rise of state capitalism with American characteristics. Interrogating the analytic rubric of the 'Investor State' in the U.S. context, this paper argues that unlike popularly assumed, such state capitalist impulses are not entirely new to American political economy but have actualized at the federal and state-levels through various vehicles of economic statecraft for a changing mix of both geostrategic/geopolitical and geoeconomic objectives since the Cold War-era, despite normative and institutional constraints. Under Trump 2.0, the Investor State has been magnified with unprecedented visibility and intrusiveness, guided by explicit imperatives of state capital accumulation and centralized decision-making under 'presidential unilateralism,' in the context of intensifying strategic rivalry with China. Bringing American and Chinese Political Economy into dialogue, this paper joins cutting-edge 'New State Capitalism' literature to challenge conventional binary geo-imaginaries and attest to the global, uneven and combined nature of new state capitalism as immanent impulses of the state in response to structural transformations of the global political economy.

detail.abstract: Urban regeneration is frequently assessed through visible outputs, including replacement housing, upgraded roads and newly installed infrastructure. Such measures provide an incomplete account of whether interventions improve everyday life. This article develops a conceptual framework for inclusive urban regeneration in India by connecting settlement assessment, housing affordability, livelihood continuity, climate-responsive design, public transport accessibility and environmental service management. It draws on selected research concerning informal settlement typologies, redevelopment, vernacular architecture, thermal comfort, passenger satisfaction, pedestrian access, green buildings and waste management. The article is a narrative synthesis and planning perspective, rather than a systematic review or empirical evaluation. Its central proposition is that the neighbourhood should be treated as a connected environment in which changes to one component can redistribute benefits and burdens across households. The proposed framework organises assessment around six domains: residential security, economic continuity, everyday accessibility, environmental comfort, service reliability and participatory governance. It links these domains to diagnosis, comparison of alternatives, implementation and post-occupancy evaluation. Particular attention is given to renters, home-based workers, people with mobility constraints and residents whose needs can be concealed by aggregate indicators. The framework offers a practical foundation for municipal planning, interdisciplinary teaching and future research, while requiring local adaptation and empirical validation before wider application.

detail.abstract: Learnable Theory's claim, broadened beyond any single application developed so far, affirms that every noun carries, for speakers and listeners alike, a geometric trace of the affordances complementary to whichever affordance the utterance selects. Complementary Semantics calls this trace the Umbra Cone, a zone of reduced activation into which the unselected affordance recedes without disappearing, and holds that it retains causal force over decisions and behavior whether or not the selected affordance carries any evaluative charge. Euphemism, the case most developed so far, is a special instance of this claim, one in which the complementary affordance also happens to be reputationally costly. This article isolates and tests the general claim directly, and asks how it relates to J-space, a form of unmotivated persistence already documented in large language models. A first test, using a concept-direction method validated in prior work, found that the predicted geometric trace appears not only for evaluatively charged complementary pairs but, with comparable or greater strength, for pairs related only by ordinary textual co-occurrence with no complementary structure at all (a beach reliably activates sunscreen; a doctor reliably activates a hospital). This threatened the specificity of every result obtained so far. A second test, grounded in Wegner's ironic process theory, resolved the threat: explicitly reinforcing a selected pole with a minimizing clause produced a large, consistent rebound in the complementary pole's activation for both evaluatively charged pairs and neutral affordance pairs, but not for pairs related by mere cooccurrence, where the same manipulation left the association unchanged or reduced it. The rebound signature, not raw co-activation, is what distinguishes genuine complementary 1 structure from ordinary distributional association, and it appears for affordances with no evaluative stakes as reliably as it appears for euphemisms.

detail.abstract: Brazil's for-profit maternity sector delivers about 80% of births by cesarean, the highest rate documented for any large health system and far above the population share of about 10% beyond which the World Health Organization finds no further gain in maternal and newborn survival. Overuse is not innocuous: unnecessary cesareans raise maternal morbidity and neonatal respiratory complications, and scheduled cesareans shift births to early-term weeks that the clinical literature links to worse newborn outcomes. We ask what sustains surgery at this scale, combining the universe of private-insurance claims, which record the physician fee billed for every delivery, with 42 million national birth records. First, the price explanation does not fit the fees: once the separately billed hourly labor-assistance fee is counted, a cesarean pays less than a vaginal delivery in Brazil's largest states, the estimated association between the billed fee gap and cesarean use switches sign across specifications, and the price response documented in the literature is far too small to account for a rate of 80%. Second, a scheduling explanation fits: cesareans concentrate on weekdays and business hours and fall on weekends and holidays, particularly when performed before labor begins. Within the same municipality and day, for-profit establishments show an additional weekend decline of 2.3 percentage points, robust to maternal composition, and for-profit births are 11.7 percentage points more likely to be early-term (37-38 weeks). The results point to a for-profit-specific supply-side scheduling margin, without separating physician convenience from ownership-specific staffing, capacity, or protocols.

detail.abstract: Global manufacturers routinely absorb three distinct classes of supply chain risk: component shortages that outrun manual material-requirements-planning (MRP) review, materials that age toward obsolescence faster than globally distributed enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems can surface, and input-cost shocks driven by fast-moving geopolitical and macroeconomic events. This paper presents a multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) framework that senses all three risk classes continuously and mitigates them not by correcting their root causes, but through controllable, intrinsic demand shaping: recommending the closest viable substitute component or finished-good the moment a risk is confirmed. The framework rests on an agent made intrinsically aware of the entire product portfolio, its bill-of-materials (BOM) structure, and the operational, engineering, and market-fit attributes of every item within it. We describe the design principles, core agent roles, and general risk-sensing process, illustrate the framework through a running example drawn from a global industrial electronics manufacturer, and detail a concrete system architecture implemented as a directed graph in LangGraph. In doing so, we explain, using the same supply chain example, the foundational graph concepts of nodes, edges, and conditional routing functions, and show how a human-approval cycle is expressed as a graph cycle rather than a one-way pipeline. We close with governance considerations and a unified set of key performance indicators (KPIs) for evaluating the framework's business impact.

title: From Knowing to Participating: AI, Situated Knowledge, and Shared Memory in Physical and Social Worlds

detail.title: From Knowing to Participating: AI, Situated Knowledge, and Shared Memory in Physical and Social Worlds

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial or non-financial competing interests related to this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this is a conceptual paper and did not involve a human-subjects study, intervention, recruitment, or systematic collection of participant data. The personal and family experiences included in the paper are used only as motivating vignettes, are paraphrased, and contain no names or clinical details.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: AI can expand the physical record of an activity while changing whether people contribute the knowledge needed to interpret it. This paper develops a conceptual account of that tension: inquiry changes relationships, and those relationships shape the evidence available to subsequent inquiry. Author-reported experiences of family remembrance, vehicle troubleshooting, and continuing medical information seeking motivate the framework. A hypothetical manufacturing example traces how additional instrumentation, perceived evaluative use, selective disclosure, and AI summaries could interact across episodes. The analysis connects situated action, transactive memory, source monitoring, information value, and organizational research on observation and concealment. Its proposed extension concerns an assistant that selects observations, assembles accounts, and uses those accounts to organize its next contribution. Two pathways distinguish suppressed disclosure from misattributed sources. Evidence-selection feedback occurs when an assembled account redirects subsequent inquiry and its resulting evidence reinforces that account. Four boundaries distinguish evidence availability, interpretation, access through relationships, and authority. Physical AI, world models, and agentic capabilities contribute through observation and action, prediction, and the organization of inquiry; their value depends on acquisition conditions and continuing human contributions. Six propositions specify trade-offs involving operational reliability, source confusion, coordination costs, disclosure, changing expertise networks, and role expansion. Prospective studies separate record completeness from diagnostic resolution and event recovery from subjective recollection. Medical collaboration serves as a transfer boundary involving individual circumstances, patient choice, professional responsibility, and longitudinal communication. The framework directs evaluation toward how participation changes both present understanding and the conditions for learning again.

detail.abstract: Classical Dow Theory holds that related markets must "confirm" each other. This paper tests that heuristic as a walk-forward-disciplined signal across a G10-FX-plus-metals universe. Two initial operationalizations fail comprehensively. A third — comparing gold's swing structure against the Australian dollar's — produces this research program's strongest single result: it clears permutation significance, achieves the maximum Deflated Sharpe Ratio reading after full multiple-testing correction, and holds up on a locked holdout. The result survives a disclosed 100-fold increase in modeled trading costs with significance essentially unchanged, but fails the study's own walk-forward-efficiency gate and rests on a shorter price history than the FX majors. A fresh reproduction attempt falls short of the original magnitude — a disclosed illustration of short-history fragility. Four follow-up studies sharpen rather than resolve the picture. The paper treats this progression as its central finding: a genuine result surviving every available test still carries real, disclosed limitations.

detail.abstract: On a 24/7/365 instant payment rail such as FedNow, autonomous liquidity management agents observe the same public signals (overnight rates such as SOFR and intraday flow) and produce Liquidity Management Transfer (LMT) recommendations. If the population of agents shares one forecasting model and one decision rule, a single shock produces synchronized LMT requests in the same direction at the same time. This is herding, the model monoculture 1 risk identified by the Financial Stability Oversight Council in its 2024 Annual Report and kept under monitoring in its 2025 Annual Report. This specification defines three things: (i) a population-level herding index built from the net internal debt ∥δ∥ 1 of a payment network under a common rate shock; (ii) design requirements that keep agent behaviour heterogeneous across institutions by construction; and (iii) a conformance test that an institution or a service provider acting for many institutions can run to verify heterogeneity without disclosing proprietary models. The payment network and the net internal debt are taken from Martinez (2023); the rate-shock engine, a Hull-White short rate with a bounded deterministic perturbation, is taken from Martinez (2025). Heterogeneity is a property of the population, not of any single institution; it cannot be purchased by one participant alone. All thresholds in this version are provisional anda reference implementation reproduces every number reported here.
